This video tells the story of what EMILYs List does best: finding the right women for the right races, helping them build winning campaigns, and making the math work in the toughest fights of the cycle.

Because our work isn't luck. It's strategy.

We recruit, train, fund, and support Democratic pro-choice women who can flip seats, protect fundamental freedoms, and build real power in states across the country. We don't just hope the political environment turns around — we work hard to make _sure_ it does.

Republican Task Force Issue: 5/18/2026
Iran Deal at the Brink

Iran made a new peace proposal to end the war on Monday, but a senior U.S. official called it insufficient and warned that if Tehran does not shift its position, the U.S. will have to continue the negotiations "through bombs." President Trump is convening a [top-level Situation Room meeting](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckL2OhCAURp9GOwwg6lhQbGM3225p7sBFb4YfAzju429mHmHrL_lyzvm5r3cgT3H7hoA6V7faZNeaz3CUSt7XHZ8UtwBPzAHKKrkcGR-YuK3Rr6K12hoLwrSoxTTNYuDDPLS75iDE2FuhsBcwPvqRo1OzkkKq6TGCaUm_r_ggZs7lPPTdPPW9c2ZQ0t2EGlWjOHjMtct4nA9PBmKF8nQpG-xMCq3Xe61HafqvRi6NXK7r6lz6jXiV997I5SyNXD4uzKT4woispoN5fKFnheoJlVJkOaXAAmKluDHKEFlMLJ7GI2RmETyjyApte22ztsdF3lMZp0bxLQD5D0z9R7uXln8BAAD__3NVgPU) with no deal in sight. The Strait of Hormuz remains closed, ceasefire conditions are deteriorating, and U.S. officials say Iran's nuclear demands remain unacceptable. Trump posted on Truth Social Sunday: "For Iran, the Clock is Ticking, and they better get moving, FAST, or there won't be anything left of them. [TIME IS OF THE ESSENCE!"](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckL2upSAUhZ8GOwxsQbGgmMbuTDul2QdQyeHHAI65b3_jfYTbrnxZa-X791pf6INP-1-MTpe2rTbbtZUrnrX5ENrhPj7tET-uRKwrMBgpk5SrNYWVd1ZbY5Gbzmk-TTOXTM6yOzQz0ggUkzA4yDefFQM1Oj7CphSAE53XTxWTfGYMZjn08zQM22akgE1xMQoiGAZXWl_ceb2DN5ga1s-Wi3G9ybEL-mjtrGT4Q2AhsNz33bfD7RcW6zE9zJPmEiyB5VkjsET8IrBwRWDxBRNN7qZnyWeuGKh1GGjL1CVLbyz0qvSBuqLtefsQfB0nItge0YefC-0Xxv5r-A4AAP__0dR6GA) ★★★
Times/Siena: Alarm Bells Ring

The New York Times/Siena poll released Monday is the political story of the week: Trump at [37% approval](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckL2yqyAUhZ8GOx3YiEpBcRu63PaUzg4bDRMUB0icvP0Z8winW8Wa9fP93OYbhhj29T9u3uS6zJRorvm1HaWGGOvDP8O-bvj0ecMyA4eh5aoV07zHWTRkyBEK13gjxlELxZVWzcMgygXpTtij4_eR9II0CtX7AQYCNzXBXFFcCc05aCU7PUq5LE71sEyiH3rWc4w-1y7743WPweFesTyXlJ3vXNqaaB61HoXJfwwsA3ueZ_cqWBPh5zIwsKWm_GFgd38WBvZIMdTgLnmVM7BcMbBiYmAp7Rip_T5v8ThyemNsM9awrwys5kJqJSXnIwPbZEPHGWIMZRhZz9cNQ_yOqn9g-DbwGwAA__-Y6H9l)--a second-term low--with 59% disapproving. Democrats lead Republicans by double digits on the [generic congressional ballot](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0LEO2yAUheGnwRsRYGPMwNDFW7p2tDBc2ygXsOCmef0qXbp3PtL5pP_Xc3v6hKmcP30G1-jYYo0btXe-OyVEuuCVypn9C1r2fVNCzVxoLpet4CaH6GKIXoYBnDTGSi201cPllmgMQJiksbOBcQ5Kyl2raKWAebdqSO57JbS0Qiirx4c143gcQU_qWOQ0T2wSHqHRo8H93jEFX8j311FbgEeoeUB3Ed2djT-YWpla6YIrIX43ptarZijw6UytnTwB_3gKF1OrXha12JFHyDU0T53_Azo_oUBLgYdazga9p1o88t0jVuJ3RRyai_cnIaY-GzaJM_v01xzoP_L9dupPAAAA__9tuoEj). The Times calls it "a crack in the polling floor"--suggesting the slide is structural, not a blip. The poll of 1,507 registered voters (May 11-15) found 64% say [the Iran war was the wrong decision](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0DGu4yAUheHV4I4IMBgoKKZxl2mntG4AB5QLtoCMt_-ULOHVR_qk8_-7b3fImOvzL5To2ti3cIRttHc5-8iII8VXrs8Cr9gK9E0wsVCmKDdbxY1PwQUfgPspOq615Yopq6bkQDKjg7GPEHb_YJ5z5oOxWnoVQIt5yu5DMcUtY8Kq-Wb1PO-7V1LshstFEskAYxu3Fs_3A7OHOqC_9qP5ePNHmdClMc5O5j9ErESsI8WUET8bEWs6Sqzx6kSsfcCI9ILhExGrMkboRdBwVMBAv1dpblDpBY2eB-LUXDivjJj7oolkzwL5y07jF4X-O_ETAAD__5pGdhU). Six months from November, this is the GOP's most alarming public data point of the cycle. ★★★
Massie's Day of Reckoning

Kentucky voters head to the polls tomorrow in the most closely watched primary of the cycle: Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., vs. Ed Gallrein, a retired Navy SEAL [backed personally by Trump](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckL2S8yAMAJ8Gd_aAMP4pKL6GLl97pUcGnGgCxgPkPHn7G6e5_rotNKuVvm7LDSnQfv-P0etct8Ult9T8ikepFEJ9-Cft94hPnyOWBTgMLVetmJY9LKJx2lmHwjZei3GcheJqVs1DO0QhthWlm61QE0yTBLc6MchxlbwfGtKXiisxcw6zkt08SrltVvWwTaIfetZzDD7XLvvjtQayuFcszy1l6zubYhP0o9ajMPmPgWFgzvPsXgVrcvi-BhiYUlN-MzC7PwsDc6RAleyFPnhbKe0XXyEMDFcMjJgYmM_5bcRSyLe_69sjU8SPsMnaHSeFQGUYWc_vESl8quofnvit4ScAAP__1B-BIA). Final polls show the race deadlocked or [Gallrein with a narrow edge](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckL2OhCAUhZ8GOw1cwZ-CYhu72XZLwwCONwIauK6Zt984j7DdSU5yfr6fx_wwGDC9vk30OtMyu93NlM94FMIQaPUbplc0m8_RlBk4dDVXtRjmFGZROe2sM8JWXou-H4XialTVqq0CIx1XStrBd_DsOiVkz8UoR_fsXV-hvqO4EiPnMKq2Gfu2XRarJCyDkJ1kkpvgMzXZH-czoDWJTNmWPVvf2D1WQa9ER2HtF4OJwXRdV5PehNGX22cw3Q0MJq4YTGJgMJ2FwXTsAQntLWndoyl1NKWgrzef6LTbu_7cr33wlnBPzUoxVFm748IQsHQ9k_wVDYbPDPoHtV8NfwEAAP__m0h7xA). Trump called Massie a "total disaster" and "vote the bum out." Prediction markets shifted sharply against Massie overnight. [CNN frames](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckLGutCAUhJ8GOw0cZdWC4m_o9m9vaY5wcMkCGmDX7NvfuI9wqykm-TLz_dyXO_rg0_YfI6lc3WJ3u9T8ikepPoT6oKdPW8Qn5YhlAQ63lstWTEsKi2isssaiMA0pMY6zkFzOsnmoCWEycl1HOVtruAPLHY2SDEG_zmgbry4Ul2LmHGbZd_PY984ZOYCbxHAb2MAxUK5dpuO1Bm8wVSxPt2dDndljE9Sj1qOw_h8DzUCf59mZlK6Ogb7oDDSXDLSYGOhjD756Uxjo7702YimeWnOF_bTrTivl2mZ6U9qoxYThU3xpsrLH6UPw5TaygW8RffgOqH_w9VbwGwAA__8tuXsS) this as Trump's most aggressive MAGA purge attempt yet--more extreme than the Cassidy ouster because Massie has one of the most conservative voting records in Congress by any ideological measure.
* * *
New Player In Michigan

2018 Republican Gubernatorial nominee Tudor Dixon is back as the spokeswoman for a new PAC. [United We Fund](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckLuunTAURL8GOiNjsMGFizR0J21KZPyALfxA9iac_H10IkW3v-3MaLS0fr3Wl4YAaf-po1MF_WqzXbHc8aoIIeDhTkh71KcrUdeVUSYI5aSf1xTWvrXKGqt70zrVT5PsOeWSt4fyXk_SCC6dl9YIPnM_iGmgfhPCjbNsQX2uKO8lpUzyoZPTMHhv-Mj83I9ibEaqgyvYFXfdWwCjE-p6-lyM60yObVAH4lWb4UfDloYtz_N0Pr-Te-qnb9hy5QAIpjZswdvmQiy8cyLF4V1SJRHMAbtO5P-OBH0nc0DaSXIPubQhGqKzZMu54if-YqnkdH_IphGD20u-kyVtUfZ6IASoYmpGukcN4R8qfsPsb8X-BgAA___ATo3F), aimed at boosting Republicans in the critical battleground of Michigan.

★★★
Trump Endorsement: A Liability?

A new Politico poll released today finds that being associated with Trump or certain special interest groups may inspire more backlash than support for candidates in competitive districts. In battleground general election contests, [Trump's endorsement could hurt](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckDHSpCAUhE-DGdbjCSoBwSZm_6YbWgw8lRLBAma9_tbMETbv6u7v-_Oz_tgQQ9p_24tMadvqs19beV93bSHGdtAZ0n7Zk8pl64qAIwfFxbymuIrOG--8Fa4jI6ZJCwVKq-4ws3Bu9EqjBDkIDV6A9gAIjl5WO-iC-VSBEhoAtRp6PQ3DtjklcZuFHCWTYCOV1he6368YnE3N1nPLxVHv8tVFc7R2Vzb8YrgwXJ7n6e8cQwsufwIMl0RPZbh8lhguoBguYma4UPK5VLooNX7nhwp_WXdGWw_-RechNSpUG99Lft-VA2iUesSuGH8_IcZQx4lJ2C8b4vdN-w95fw3-CwAA___sSX1h) more than it helps--a finding that reframes the entire GOP midterm calculus: his coattails win primaries and cost generals.

★★★
Trump Endorsement Proves Decisive

Trump-backed Julie Letlow advanced to a runoff against John Fleming as incumbent Louisiana Senator [Bill Cassidy](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0D2upDAQBODTQGbkHwxD4GATstl0Q9TgBqxpG2Q3y-7tn2aCd4AXl1Sqr_48pycECmn7DRFd5nXyh584X_EsHIh4x1dIW4QX5ghl0lJ3QlqhHlOiSdXe-cWDWmp0qu8HZaUdbL070_W6nRWi9FYa-TAoe49mmVf0neq7Orh3lbRqkFIP1jRDb8y6LrbV60O1XVu1EggzNxnPa6awQGIor_XICzbLEWtyO_NZKvOr0mOlx_u-m_X4l_Au77zSY0QfoNLjhyN2zEAevdiOU3yjBB1XKAESiIIJGEXGchEXkYGZUJyQ-b_AwjBTKHvExHV2_rwDUShdX7VyixDos4l_cOFfp78CAAD__9U3hNo) became the first Senator to lose re-nomination since 2012. Cassidy voted to convict Trump in the January 6 impeachment trial, and Trump committed to removing him from office.

* * *
Reconciliation Rewrite Begins

Senate Republicans released new reconciliation text this week as they begin the rewrite process after the Byrd bath knocked out the White House ballroom security provision and other challenged items. [This week is the official redraft](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0DuOpDAQgOHTmIyWXcY8AgebkPWmG6LCj6ZEYZDtXjS3H_UcYeJf-oL_33N5IjGl1188gs01Lv70S83v4yqVmOsWdkqvA_eQDywLSOhbaVo1LokX1XjrnUflmmDVMEzKSDOZZrPr6NGvgx7lqkA7LSeIk46jk53pe3QN2Q8ljZqkhMnoxzRoHaMzHcRRdX0nOokccn3kcL1XJoepYtnjmV14uPNo2G61XkXoPwJmAXM-mR0yf6KA-cMLmKURMKtRwFw3Ku0dwt7m4M7kiAkrnaldibnN4c5UQ2nfyYd845eAucnWXzcxU-kH0cnXgfTDN_UXq_5b-A4AAP__1al4Fw)--members are back at the drawing board negotiating what stays in the bill. The "Big Beautiful One" now faces a second round of parliamentarian scrutiny once revised text is finalized, with a June 1 deadline for immigration enforcement funding.

★★★
The Third Bill Fantasy

House conservatives are already floating a third reconciliation vehicle--for Pentagon funding and fraud programs--by the August recess, while the first "Big Beautiful One" is still being rewritten in the Senate. [A vocal faction wants to add a third vehicle](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0LGOhCAQxvGnwc4NoKgUFNfY7bVXmlkYdLIjGMTb17_sPsJ1X_Ilv-L_c1_uQExp_YYdXalxCTkstVz7cVZirhs-Ka07PLHscC5a6qGVplXTknhRTXDBB1C-QafG0SojjTXN5jqIJgRtpQaUMYzWdtY8vNZqNGawqiH3pqRRVkptTXezY9fF6E2v46T6oRe9BMZSbwWP68HkIVU4nzEXjzef94bdVutxiu5L6FnouW64EfP7E3re8o4JX-dnXicKPZtpkqYf2jUfbUGfkycmqJRT-yDm9sBUYc2pjQWuIPTcFBeOFzHTOYyil-sO9PGb-o9Uv07_BQAA__8Z9HiO) while leadership is still struggling to pass the first. At some point, governing requires actually passing something.

★★★
Kennedy: No Work, No Pay

The Senate unanimously passed Sen. John Kennedy's, R-La., resolution requiring senators' pay to be withheld during government shutdowns--after Congress received full paychecks during 119 days of shutdowns between October 2025 and May 2026 while federal employees missed checks. The measure [won't take effect until after November](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckD0O3CAUhE-DOyx-jL0UFGncbdqU1jM828iALWCX5PbRbpEDpB2NPs18v57LE3zwaf8JEU2u2-Iut9T8inepPoR64OnTHuHEHKEsgomRMkX5Y0lh4Z0zzjrgtkPDp0lzxZRW3WE2ySfOmWTaaiWRCekU6BVWGCfO0HXefFBMcc2Y0Er2epJy26waxPbgwziQgUHAXPuM92sN3kKqUM7tyhZ7e8UumKPWuxD5g4iZiLm11jcoh097vRL-hugT5k-ViDlhK0TMBRNUJGIe1DhxPf6LKLg3JIuFrj4EuobLnjRA-x6nN_yh-_XGnCKmSsvxqu5q6UPssnF38yH4Mk5kYHsEH7776n_ofBvxNwAA__-8Noat), but sets up accountability framing for any future shutdown fight.

body:
We are less than $10K from meeting our fundraising goal!

| | | | | [|
---](https://hicksforsenate.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e3e4c73c4cf0c85a1ab7cfa3e&id=49dc1458ed&e=1074427541)
| | | | | |
Dear friends,
As you may have heard, **Senate District 3 is considered the #1 targeted race in the State of Oregon**. All eyes are on this critical swing seat as our victory will end the one-party supermajority. This race will really come down to you...turnout and aggressive grassroots support. As I'm sure you've seen, turnout is very low in Oregon thus far. name: Mark Ronchetti
subject: The Dems are at war. Rubio just opened a 16-point lead.
body:
Plus: $165 billion Project Jupiter is coming. Here's the catch | New episode for dpwillis67@gmail.com

| | | | | |
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/tXNaUrXPHbx?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | | | | |
Marco Rubio just opened a 16-point lead over JD Vance for 2028.
Meanwhile a former Democratic governor went on national TV and torched her own party. A former Albuquerque mayor went after a fellow Democrat in the Journal. AOC is leading the Democratic primary at 26%. One party is finding its next leader. The other is still fighting over its last one.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/mbo36RXBscB?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| |
🚨 **DEMOCRATS ARE AT WAR WITH THEMSELVES**
Christine Gregoire — former Washington governor — went on national TV and torched her own party. The four-word phrase she used about Democratic spending should end up in every GOP ad this cycle.
Then former Albuquerque Mayor Marty Chavez wrote an op-ed going after Sam Bregman in the Journal. Democrat-on-Democrat, in print.
And the 2028 Democratic field? AOC 26. Buttigieg 22. Newsom 21. Harris 12.
**Their frontrunner has never run anything.

** 🔥 **RUBIO 45, VANCE 29 — A 22-POINT SWING IN FIVE MONTHS**
Five months ago, JD Vance led Marco Rubio by 24 points. Now Rubio leads by 16.
Vance has been quiet. Rubio has been everywhere. Then Trump went to the Rose Garden and floated a Vance-Rubio "dream team" ticket.
The crowd's reaction tells you everything.
---
| [Stream Episode Now](https://us.list-manage.com/E447dymUHTR?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| |
💰 **$165 BILLION IS COMING TO DOÑA ANA COUNTY**
Project Jupiter. Oracle. OpenAI. A 1,400-acre AI data center campus in Santa Teresa.
Seven in 10 Americans say they oppose AI data centers near where they live. A separate project near Fort Bliss would need more power than every El Paso Electric customer combined.
That's the number that should stop you cold.
Florida's Ron DeSantis is doing this differently. Mark walks through what Santa Fe should be studying — before the next one lands here.

🇨🇳 **A CHINESE SPY WAS ELECTED MAYOR. NBC IS WORRIED ABOUT SOMETHING ELSE.**
Eileen Wang, mayor of Arcadia, California, just pleaded guilty to acting as an illegal agent of the Chinese government.
NBC's tweet didn't lead with the espionage. It led with "anti-Asian discrimination" concerns. We walk through, line by line, how a major network frames a story like this.

🎬 **TMZ TRIED TO BURY SPENCER PRATT. HE DIDN'T BLINK.**
Harvey Levin spent ten minutes trying to get the LA mayoral candidate to admit the Airstream on his burned-out Pacific Palisades lot isn't really his house. Pratt's response is the part we want you to see.
---
| [Stream Episode Now](https://us.list-manage.com/SA7EkHSr3G8?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| |
PLUS: Three NM Republican write-ins (Larry Marker, Joshua Lawrence, James Ellison) each need 2,351 votes to make the November ballot. Jim Jordan on CNN with Kaitlan Collins — it does not go well. A septic truck loses a fight with a train in Virginia. And a bear manhandles Mark's trail camera.

# **VOTE on TUESDAY, MAY 19th!**
Tuesday, May 19th, is election day! Make your voice heard and go vote. **[Find your Philadelphia polling locations ](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100171784.172866.41&gen=1&mailing_linkid=17032)** **[Find your Montgomery County polling locations ](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100171784.172866.41&gen=1&mailing_linkid=17033)**
* * *
## **Not Sure Who 's on the Ballot?**
[**View Philadelphia's sample ballot HERE**](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100171784.172866.41&gen=1&mailing_linkid=17034) [**View Montgomery County's sample ballot HERE**](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100171784.172866.41&gen=1&mailing_linkid=17035)
* * *
## **Important Voting Information **
* You can [look up your polling place online](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100171784.172866.41&gen=1&mailing_linkid=17036)
* Polls will be open on **May 19th from 7AM to 8PM**
* The busiest times to vote are in the morning and evening, so plan ahead or try going at a less busy time
* If this is your first time voting, you must bring a photo or non-photo ID
* If you encounter any problems at the polls, call **1-877-868-3772**. The PA Department of State will be able to answer your questions and help with any issues.
* You can also reach he Philadelphia County Board of Elections at** 215-686-3469**

Some doctors say many supermarket bottles are so heavily processed, they contain far fewer of the polyphenols people expect from olive oil in the first place.

Many people never realize there’s a difference until they learn what’s actually been stripped out of common store-bought oils.

Dr. Gundry points to one type of olive oil sourced from harsh Moroccan conditions that may contain dramatically higher levels of the compounds most people are looking for.

body:
| | | | | [|

| | | | | | Hi –
I don’t know about you, but I miss the days that I didn’t have to think about what our government or president was up to for days at a time. I wish it was that easy to not care, but I do – and something tells me you do too.
I have to be honest with you: among so many dumpster fires happening in our country right now, seeing the nationwide redistricting battle and all-out assault on the Voting Rights Act over recent weeks has outraged me — and it should anger you too.

Ruling by ruling, conservative courts and state legislatures are dismantling what generations of Americans bled, marched, and died to build. They are handing power-hungry politicians the ability to choose their own voters, escape accountability, and silence the voices of our Black and Brown neighbors.
The Voting Rights Act was a promise to every American that their voice would count. It was signed into law by LBJ, who was born right here in TX-21 in the Texas Hill Country. He used his power to give voice to the powerless and to fulfill the promise of equal participation. That’s our legacy, and I’m running for Congress to defend it.
The nationwide redistricting battle started right here in Texas. Republicans spent months trying to rig the Texas map to shield themselves from accountability and appease Trump, but little did they know they would make TX-21 more winnable.
[**Help it backfire.**](https://us.list-manage.com/yIV3vcvuv6T?e=395a33a3d2&c2id=2ea96fa4e6b867a41c995b28450e35c7)
Three years ago, I gave up my job, healthcare, and home to run for this seat because I believe we deserve leaders who fight for people, not power. More than 153,000 bipartisan voters trusted that message – even with the odds stacked against us.
This year we’re going to finish the job. And I’m so proud to have you on my side.
I'm not self-funded. I don't have a billionaire's checkbook. What I have is you — and a moment that comes once in a generation.
Don't let this moment pass and [**make a donation today**](https://us.list-manage.com/pEPwXvFYgga?e=395a33a3d2&c2id=2ea96fa4e6b867a41c995b28450e35c7) to ensure we win. Your contribution isn't just supporting a campaign – it's a vote for someone who will be a voice for the powerless and who isn’t afraid to hold the powerful accountable. Let’s win!

clean_body: | | | | | | | | | | | Hi – I don’t know about you, but I miss the days that I didn’t have to think about what our government or president was up to for days at a time. I wish it was that easy to not care, but I do – and something tells me you do too. I have to be honest with you: among so many dumpster fires happening in our country right now, seeing the nationwide redistricting battle and all-out assault on the Voting Rights Act over recent weeks has outraged me — and it should anger you too. Ruling by ruling, conservative courts and state legislatures are dismantling what generations of Americans bled, marched, and died to build. They are handing power-hungry politicians the ability to choose their own voters, escape accountability, and silence the voices of our Black and Brown neighbors. The Voting Rights Act was a promise to every American that their voice would count. It was signed into law by LBJ, who was born right here in TX-21 in the Texas Hill Country. He used his power to give voice to the powerless and to fulfill the promise of equal participation. That’s our legacy, and I’m running for Congress to defend it. The nationwide redistricting battle started right here in Texas. Republicans spent months trying to rig the Texas map to shield themselves from accountability and appease Trump, but little did they know they would make TX-21 more winnable. Three years ago, I gave up my job, healthcare, and home to run for this seat because I believe we deserve leaders who fight for people, not power. More than 153,000 bipartisan voters trusted that message – even with the odds stacked against us. This year we’re going to finish the job. And I’m so proud to have you on my side. I'm not self-funded. I don't have a billionaire's checkbook. What I have is you — and a moment that comes once in a generation. Don't let this moment pass and to ensure we win. Your contribution isn't just supporting a campaign – it's a vote for someone who will be a voice for the powerless and who isn’t afraid to hold the powerful accountable. Let’s win! | | | | | | | | | | | Copyright (C) 2026 Dr. Kristin Hook for Congress. All rights reserved.

## Trump Drops IRS Suit to Get $1.8B Fund
President Trump [dropped his $10 billion lawsuit](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOrCAYRp8GOw0gKBYUt7Gb225pEH7GfxfUAA6Zt984r7D1l5yT73w9lofBgPvzv4mgiz-WHWoOUAqkpaQrnsFUbxL4a3fxyj_hyJAXTvnQUtmyaXEGw3sRjdMegEPfgGbjODEle8GaTTu19mYV0yC9GiZhODVSWQmej84AXRvUN41KNjFKlVTdJKwVilrje0m5GYmg4LAcqfs-cC8b-PA-XpA6e8Qm6K2UM5P-H-Ez4XOttbP7au-R8PlGEz5TSfjMFOHz51PrMEfMucWU22BqvrB0W4mhSdqdFUPAPNzeZzQYPp7ypzgvzX8DAAD__8pHeHo) against the IRS on Monday in exchange for the Justice Department creating a $1.776 billion fund for people who claim they were wrongly targeted under the Biden administration. A [five-member commission](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGO4yAQxvGnwR3RAAbjguKkk7tcc1ptaREYEnaxsQDHytuvnFfYeqTR__d9XuerjSmu9392QdNCnlc8asLWsMyt7MuW7BFswbCvftnrd8oV68yBKwqSsnH2NqbX3HfeBESOokPDhmFkWoqedQ-DvQeOgxRajdxxJUctHGilHGPglOiiOb-BZCMD0FJfxt65XoOzQUjgdiA9oI8tl8tXjmt7YEiv_MRycXnpknm0tlUi_hA-ET7ZmzsF543w6eM_4dObQV3eS6Phja10S3at1Je8UQY3muxR99hoLJXwqbZcXkRM0RPxlwkBSkEvumL8dsSUYlVn032xMb0b2q-Gexr-EwAA__-GPYDv) appointed by the attorney general will run the new Anti-Weaponization Fund, and Trump can remove any member. The money comes from the Treasury's Judgment Fund, a taxpayer-backed account used to pay government settlements. Trump can't receive payouts himself, but [Jan. 6 defendants potentially could](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2O6yAQhZ8Gd1iA_3BBEV3JXW67pTWxh4RdDBaMw2affuW8wpajOTr6zvdxna_gvAv3_7ChIRvngCV7JMI0Uzq23UOxkNAeYd2O_OVjxjwroXouOi7HeQXnX3NbrcYiKmwqNHIYRqm7ppXVw2B3s_1oWz3oYehRDlJDC0I3nVDNeBOVM2eb6OQohdCdrsd2WVotFrBnBgbWClwdxVR_Rhfogda_4hNTvcSt8uZBtGfWXJiamJpKKfWWw_ljasLAj8zUtMWAL6Ymgm887_cyvqa4Z-5S5h5KPhxxinxJCIRc6huHQI4XhD0G9wPkYuCnBqYmSPxyUc2x_1urZNa9OO9d7k_U-wbOv9HoTz6fRv0GAAD__5fSiyU). Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche, who previously represented Trump in criminal matters, signed the deal, which expires in December 2028.
## Energy Merger Will Create World's Biggest Utility
Energy companies NextEra and Dominion [announced a nearly $67 billion merger](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DuO2zAUheHVUB0FPiSKKlgECNRN2pTCFe-lzQwfBkWP4t0HzhamPsCPD-f3x_4BMcVy-wWZXA91L3SdiXqntvf2zI8EV4BG4VkwP8_PVE86dyWU4WLmct0RYnrt04AuECnSAzm5LKu0s57kcHcepQw0w-GNATMhan1MwSx2JaWRpiG6d03McpVC2NmO6-T9ZIWHoGehYGGTIIy9tvFPjaXfKaRX_aI2-pqH5O69P06mfzC1MbVd1zX6cvj3yNT2TjO1iZmpTVqmtkJ_OzXghYhjzbHEWjgVarcXR47QgXsqnRqHON57Tkxv-az-MyLTP4WeF3vYQ_p1Mf4wQmuzkiSJgAY1DM3h44opxdO83bcMMf139m-d--XUvwAAAP__YUyMFQ) Monday that will create the world's largest regulated electric utility, serving 10 million customers across Florida, Virginia, and the Carolinas. The companies say [scale is the point](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1urDAQRp_GdKzsMQZTuLgN3d42JfLCAJP4B5lhN7x9tHmF1J_0naPzcR_vngKl9b-P6HjJY8LXEZAZy8jljHvwr8UXXM40x_P4CvnAYwQJbS1Nrfpx9hSusalmtyAC6gqd6rpeWaMbVW3OL9BLpVo7ddMDUHujW_sw2jQPo6XVFbn3mzSqV1JaY299M02NlZNftJHgO9FInIlzuX1mSrzhEq78xHKbcqyC25j3Q-h_AgYBA2-4UQjvTcCw50DTJWDAhGW9akxPKjlFTCxgMNZqBaZO-M1YfD3nSIlyqk-mQHzVEcuKRcBQFTfvLwqBjvbts0ZPv4yK_xTt6eAnAAD__5N8gbw): larger combined operations mean more efficient construction and financing, which they argue will eventually lead to lower bills for customers amid surging demand for AI data centers. The combined company will operate under NextEra's name, though Dominion's brand will remain in place for its local operations in Virginia and the Carolinas. The all-stock deal is expected to close in 12 to 18 months.
## Human Beats Robot in 10-Hour Factory Challenge
A human intern named Aime outpaced a humanoid robot from Figure AI in a live-streamed 10-hour parcel-sorting challenge in California, finishing with 12,924 packages to the machine's 12,732, a margin of 0.4 seconds per package. Here I am again talking about stock trading, because President Trump's latest financial disclosures came out, and it sure as hell looks like the party is happening and we are not invited.
Please Support The Angry Democrat
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..6Puv-vNhI9RXV5ziYGEmQ_XDqMaX6anf1WSJqaitpzk?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=198277514)
Not that I even want to be invited. What I am saying is that this looks like a massive cluster of self-enrichment, conflicts of interest, insider access, and institutional corruption. And at some point, I have to wonder how much longer people can keep pretending they do not see it.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c927ba00-bbea-47c5-96d4-f1733cdf8799?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This is not just some niche ethics story for political nerds. [Yale's Program on Climate Change Communication found](https://substack.com/redirect/611cde21-2a2a-4781-85f7-f4866064089c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that government corruption was the top public worry in the United States, with 54% of Americans saying they were very worried about it, ahead of the cost of living at 48% and the economy at 47%.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/870336df-7543-4ebf-8a09-1f4431b82980?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
So when people say voters do not care about corruption, I think that is bullshit. They **do** care. They may not always use the same language. They may not follow every disclosure filing. They may not know what an OGE Form 278-T is (_The OGE Form 278-T or, Periodic Transaction Report, is a mandatory federal ethics form used by senior government officials to disclose financial transactions, such as the purchase, sale, or exchange of securities_). But they know the system feels rigged. They know the people in power seem to get richer while everyone else gets told to tighten their belt.
And they are not wrong.
* * *
### This Is Not Just a Trump Problem
Democrats are going to use Trump's financial disclosures as more proof that Trump is corrupt and in office for self-enrichment. **Of course he is!!!!!** I have written about that plenty of times, and I think the evidence keeps stacking up. Read about it below.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/4f1a61cb-e485-4f8a-83b7-9777c85c417e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |
#### [Trump's Swamp is Monetized](https://substack.com/redirect/4f1a61cb-e485-4f8a-83b7-9777c85c417e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [The Angry Democrat](https://substack.com/profile/102996536-the-angry-democrat)| | *
---|---|---
| Apr 13
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/4f1a61cb-e485-4f8a-83b7-9777c85c417e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
But this turns into party politics way too quickly when the bigger issue is that this is a uniparty of corruption. The rot is not limited to one side.
Nancy Pelosi defended members of Congress being allowed to trade stocks by saying, "We're a free-market economy. They (congress) should be able to participate in that."
[](https://substack.com/redirect/41cbe32a-12bb-4456-b597-d2ca369a2f07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Mike Johnson](https://substack.com/redirect/f6859127-2d9b-4caa-a49f-16e27b63736e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) has also pumped the brakes on banning congressional stock trading, arguing that a ban could discourage good people from running for office, even after previously saying he supported a ban because of the "appearance of impropriety."
So there it is.
Different parties. Different speakers. Same basic posture.
Congress needs to get the bag. Members need to be able to make money. Do not make public office too restrictive. Do not scare away "good people." Let them participate in the markets.
And what does that really mean?
It means the people running the government are allowed to use proximity to power, policy, regulation, classified briefings, committee work, agency relationships, and insider timing to get filthy rich, while lying to the rest of us that it is just normal investing.
That is fucking insane. [Unusual Whales](https://open.substack.com/users/22534812-unusual-whales?utm_source=mentions)
[](https://substack.com/redirect/7f0b9288-f5fe-4d03-9302-6886e27d4369?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
### Should Congress Be Paid More? That Does Not Mean They Should Trade Stocks
I want to be clear about something because I have said this before and I still believe it.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/8a2271eb-ac19-4f29-9452-0fa02888c83c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |
#### [The Salary Freeze That is Breaking Congress](https://substack.com/redirect/8a2271eb-ac19-4f29-9452-0fa02888c83c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [The Angry Democrat](https://substack.com/profile/102996536-the-angry-democrat)| | *
---|---|---
| Feb 13
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/8a2271eb-ac19-4f29-9452-0fa02888c83c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Congress should probably be paid more. Their salaries have lost spending power. Many members have to live in two places. They are supposed to represent hundreds of thousands of people. And if we want ordinary people to be able to serve, we should make public service financially realistic.
Mike Johnson has a point there.
But that is a different argument from letting members of Congress trade individual stocks while they are shaping the rules of the economy. Those are not the same thing.
Pay Congress more if that is the problem. Create housing allowances if that is the problem. Reform the size of the House if that is the problem. Hell, maybe we should revisit what representation is supposed to look like when one member of Congress represents far too many people and the whole thing has become completely detached from the original constitutional scale.
But do not tell me the answer is letting elected officials trade stocks while they have access to information, influence, and policy levers that regular Americans will never touch.
* * *
### **NOW** the Executive Branch Is in the Game Too
Please Support The Angry Democrat
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..6Puv-vNhI9RXV5ziYGEmQ_XDqMaX6anf1WSJqaitpzk?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=198277514)
And now, with Trump's latest disclosures, we are not just talking about Congress anymore. We are talking about the executive branch.
[Reuters](https://substack.com/redirect/a41dd39c-f96d-40af-a168-428af862805f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) reported that President Trump disclosed at least $220 million in financial transactions involving U.S. corporate securities during the first quarter of 2026, with the disclosure range putting the total as high as around $750 million. Let me repeat that for everyone in the back. **THE FIRST QUARTER**
Now, the Trump Organization says these holdings are managed through fully discretionary accounts controlled by third-party financial institutions, and that Trump, his family, and the Trump Organization do not select, direct, approve, or get advance notice of individual investment decisions.
[| | | | | Ricardo
---
@Ric_RTP
Trump just got exposed for running the biggest insider trading operation in American history. Nancy Pelosi traded $5 million in stocks and Congress lost its mind. Trump literally executed $750 MILLION worth of stock trades in ONE quarter while being President. His ethics
| 1:14 PM * May 17, 2026 * 1.55M Views1.41K Replies * 14.2K Reposts * 33.1K Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/e59e3b6b-04c2-416f-a446-b55af4176342?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**But I keep coming back to the same standard I have written about before.**
In the judicial world, there is this old ethics principle that a judge should avoid not only impropriety, but also the appearance of impropriety. The U.S. Courts' Code of Conduct says an appearance of impropriety exists when reasonable minds, knowing the relevant facts, would conclude that a judge's honesty, integrity, impartiality, temperament, or fitness to serve is impaired.
Even if Trump's portfolio was technically managed by outside brokers, a president holding and trading hundreds of millions of dollars in securities tied to companies affected by his own administration creates a massive appearance-of-impropriety problem.
* * *
### **Trump Has Monetized the White House**
Donald Trump has monetized the White House in a way that is almost too obvious to even describe without sounding ridiculous.
It feels like he brought in a team to walk through the entire federal government and asked: Where are the products? What can we sell? What can be branded? What can be routed through a family-connected business? What can be turned into a financial instrument? What can be converted into access?
Crypto. Stablecoins. Executive orders. Pardons. Foreign policy. Regulatory capture. Government contracts. Military leverage. Public statements. White House events. Everything is a storefront.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/37fa77da-488f-4339-bc75-c561699644f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
And now people are looking at the timing of public statements, policy decisions, and stock positions and asking the obvious question.
Is this all coincidence?
We should not have to ask whether the president is governing for the country or trading around the country.
p.s. I will answer that question for you. No. No it isn't coincidence.
* * *
### This Is a Democratic AND Republican Crisis.
No. Actually, this is a democracy and the republic crisis.
This is not a left-right issue. It is not just Trump. It is not just Pelosi. It is not just Mike Johnson. It is not just congressional stock trading. It is not just the executive branch.
It is a crisis of whether representative government still represents the people, or whether it has become a wealth machine for insiders.
It is a crisis when members of Congress trade stocks while sitting on committees that affect industries.
It is a crisis when party leaders defend the right to trade because lawmakers supposedly need more money.
It is a crisis when the president's financial disclosures show hundreds of millions of dollars in transactions tied to companies affected by the government he runs.
It is a crisis when the public looks at all of this and knows, correctly, that if a normal person did anything even remotely similar inside their job, they would be fired, investigated, or both.
**Government officials are using the will of the people, taxpayer dollars, the United States military, foreign policy, and the economic might of this country to benefit a very small group of people. Their friends. Their donors. Their business partners. Their families. Themselves.**
**That is corruption.**
**And I am sick of people acting like it is only corruption when the other party does it.**
* * *
### The Solution
The solution should be simple.
Ban members of Congress, presidents, vice presidents, cabinet officials, senior executive branch officials, judges, Supreme Court justices, and their spouses from trading individual stocks while in office.
Require real blind trusts, diversified mutual funds, or divestment where necessary. Ban government officials from holding individual securities in companies they regulate, contract with, subsidize, investigate, rule on, appoint people to oversee, or publicly promote.
And stop pretending disclosure is enough.
Disclosure is not accountability. Disclosure is not prevention. Disclosure is not ethics. Disclosure is just the public getting to see the receipt after the insiders already made the trade.
If elected officials think they cannot survive on their salary without trading around their own power, then raise the salary and close the loophole. Or... wait for it... live pay check to pay check like 60% of the USA!
Do not use underpayment as an excuse for legalized corruption. If you are making policy that moves markets, you should not be personally trading in those markets.
And maybe this is where people need to start thinking bigger. There is no direct national citizen petition that can force a constitutional amendment by itself. A citizen-led campaign could pressure Congress, pressure state legislatures, force candidates to take a position, organize state-level ballot efforts where allowed, and build the kind of public demand that makes this impossible to ignore. Maybe we need to collect signatures across country.
Check out [Political Integrity Project](https://open.substack.com/users/431030161-political-integrity-project?utm_source=mentions) & [https://integrityindex.us](https://substack.com/redirect/8f1b89f6-87cd-42e1-a9d1-4f2f06c803b2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
This is not just unethical. **It is a national security issue.** A government that normalizes corruption can be bought, bent, manipulated, and redirected away from the people it is supposed to serve.
So we can keep pretending this is just politics, or we can admit the whole damn system is infected. Federal and Local.

clean_body: Trump, Pelosi, Congress, and the bipartisan defense of self-enrichment | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more ? We need to find other ANGRY DEMOCRATS. Please consider sharing and subscribing to fuel the ANGER for change. Trump, Pelosi, Congress, and the bipartisan defense of self-enrichment | | | May 19 | | | | | | | | | | | | Here I am again talking about stock trading, because President Trump's latest financial disclosures came out, and it sure as hell looks like the party is happening and we are not invited. Please Support The Angry Democrat Not that I even want to be invited. What I am saying is that this looks like a massive cluster of self-enrichment, conflicts of interest, insider access, and institutional corruption. And at some point, I have to wonder how much longer people can keep pretending they do not see it. | | ---|---|--- This is not just some niche ethics story for political nerds. that government corruption was the top public worry in the United States, with 54% of Americans saying they were very worried about it, ahead of the cost of living at 48% and the economy at 47%. | | ---|---|--- So when people say voters do not care about corruption, I think that is bullshit. They do care. They may not always use the same language. They may not follow every disclosure filing. They may not know what an OGE Form 278-T is (The OGE Form 278-T or, Periodic Transaction Report, is a mandatory federal ethics form used by senior government officials to disclose financial transactions, such as the purchase, sale, or exchange of securities). But they know the system feels rigged. They know the people in power seem to get richer while everyone else gets told to tighten their belt. And they are not wrong. This Is Not Just a Trump Problem Democrats are going to use Trump's financial disclosures as more proof that Trump is corrupt and in office for self-enrichment. Of course he is!!!!! I have written about that plenty of times, and I think the evidence keeps stacking up. Read about it below. | | | | | | | ---|---|--- | Apr 13 | But this turns into party politics way too quickly when the bigger issue is that this is a uniparty of corruption. The rot is not limited to one side. Nancy Pelosi defended members of Congress being allowed to trade stocks by saying, "We're a free-market economy. They (congress) should be able to participate in that." has also pumped the brakes on banning congressional stock trading, arguing that a ban could discourage good people from running for office, even after previously saying he supported a ban because of the "appearance of impropriety." So there it is. Different parties. Different speakers. Same basic posture. Congress needs to get the bag. Members need to be able to make money. Do not make public office too restrictive. Do not scare away "good people." Let them participate in the markets. And what does that really mean? It means the people running the government are allowed to use proximity to power, policy, regulation, classified briefings, committee work, agency relationships, and insider timing to get filthy rich, while lying to the rest of us that it is just normal investing. That is fucking insane. Should Congress Be Paid More? That Does Not Mean They Should Trade Stocks I want to be clear about something because I have said this before and I still believe it. | | | | | | | ---|---|--- | Feb 13 | Congress should probably be paid more. Their salaries have lost spending power. Many members have to live in two places. They are supposed to represent hundreds of thousands of people. And if we want ordinary people to be able to serve, we should make public service financially realistic. Mike Johnson has a point there. But that is a different argument from letting members of Congress trade individual stocks while they are shaping the rules of the economy. Those are not the same thing. Pay Congress more if that is the problem. Create housing allowances if that is the problem. Reform the size of the House if that is the problem. Hell, maybe we should revisit what representation is supposed to look like when one member of Congress represents far too many people and the whole thing has become completely detached from the original constitutional scale. But do not tell me the answer is letting elected officials trade stocks while they have access to information, influence, and policy levers that regular Americans will never touch. NOW the Executive Branch Is in the Game Too Please Support The Angry Democrat And now, with Trump's latest disclosures, we are not just talking about Congress anymore. We are talking about the executive branch. reported that President Trump disclosed at least $220 million in financial transactions involving U.S. corporate securities during the first quarter of 2026, with the disclosure range putting the total as high as around $750 million. Let me repeat that for everyone in the back. THE FIRST QUARTER Now, the Trump Organization says these holdings are managed through fully discretionary accounts controlled by third-party financial institutions, and that Trump, his family, and the Trump Organization do not select, direct, approve, or get advance notice of individual investment decisions. But I keep coming back to the same standard I have written about before. In the judicial world, there is this old ethics principle that a judge should avoid not only impropriety, but also the appearance of impropriety. The U.S. Courts' Code of Conduct says an appearance of impropriety exists when reasonable minds, knowing the relevant facts, would conclude that a judge's honesty, integrity, impartiality, temperament, or fitness to serve is impaired. Even if Trump's portfolio was technically managed by outside brokers, a president holding and trading hundreds of millions of dollars in securities tied to companies affected by his own administration creates a massive appearance-of-impropriety problem. Trump Has Monetized the White House Donald Trump has monetized the White House in a way that is almost too obvious to even describe without sounding ridiculous. It feels like he brought in a team to walk through the entire federal government and asked: Where are the products? What can we sell? What can be branded? What can be routed through a family-connected business? What can be turned into a financial instrument? What can be converted into access? Crypto. Stablecoins. Executive orders. Pardons. Foreign policy. Regulatory capture. Government contracts. Military leverage. Public statements. White House events. Everything is a storefront. And now people are looking at the timing of public statements, policy decisions, and stock positions and asking the obvious question. Is this all coincidence? We should not have to ask whether the president is governing for the country or trading around the country. p.s. I will answer that question for you. No. No it isn't coincidence. This Is a Democratic AND Republican Crisis. No. Actually, this is a democracy and the republic crisis. This is not a left-right issue. It is not just Trump. It is not just Pelosi. It is not just Mike Johnson. It is not just congressional stock trading. It is not just the executive branch. It is a crisis of whether representative government still represents the people, or whether it has become a wealth machine for insiders. It is a crisis when members of Congress trade stocks while sitting on committees that affect industries. It is a crisis when party leaders defend the right to trade because lawmakers supposedly need more money. It is a crisis when the president's financial disclosures show hundreds of millions of dollars in transactions tied to companies affected by the government he runs. It is a crisis when the public looks at all of this and knows, correctly, that if a normal person did anything even remotely similar inside their job, they would be fired, investigated, or both. Government officials are using the will of the people, taxpayer dollars, the United States military, foreign policy, and the economic might of this country to benefit a very small group of people. Their friends. Their donors. Their business partners. Their families. Themselves. That is corruption. And I am sick of people acting like it is only corruption when the other party does it. The Solution The solution should be simple. Ban members of Congress, presidents, vice presidents, cabinet officials, senior executive branch officials, judges, Supreme Court justices, and their spouses from trading individual stocks while in office. Require real blind trusts, diversified mutual funds, or divestment where necessary. Ban government officials from holding individual securities in companies they regulate, contract with, subsidize, investigate, rule on, appoint people to oversee, or publicly promote. And stop pretending disclosure is enough. Disclosure is not accountability. Disclosure is not prevention. Disclosure is not ethics. Disclosure is just the public getting to see the receipt after the insiders already made the trade. If elected officials think they cannot survive on their salary without trading around their own power, then raise the salary and close the loophole. Or... wait for it... live pay check to pay check like 60% of the USA! Do not use underpayment as an excuse for legalized corruption. If you are making policy that moves markets, you should not be personally trading in those markets. And maybe this is where people need to start thinking bigger. There is no direct national citizen petition that can force a constitutional amendment by itself. A citizen-led campaign could pressure Congress, pressure state legislatures, force candidates to take a position, organize state-level ballot efforts where allowed, and build the kind of public demand that makes this impossible to ignore. Maybe we need to collect signatures across country. Check out & This is not just unethical. It is a national security issue. A government that normalizes corruption can be bought, bent, manipulated, and redirected away from the people it is supposed to serve. So we can keep pretending this is just politics, or we can admit the whole damn system is infected. Federal and Local. Stay Angry Join otherANGRY DEMOCRATS** by support Matt's work. We cannot afford another term of Lying Lisa Baker...

| | | | | [|

| | | | | | Peter,

**Polls are NOW open until 8:00 PM tonight. As long as you are in line by 8:00 PM, you can cast your ballot for the only proven conservative fighter in this race!**

This election will not only determine who represents us in the Pennsylvania Senate, but also the direction of our commonwealth for generations to come.

We can either maintain the status quo, which is taxing and spending Pennsylvania into poverty, or **we can elect a real conservative Republican who will fight for our families, our freedoms, and our wallets.**

We cannot afford a Senator who is weak on our constitutionally protected rights.

We cannot afford to send a career politician back to Harrisburg who refuses to tackle high costs through eliminating taxes and cutting spending.

We cannot afford another term of Lying Lisa Baker.

We need to elect a political outsider who will never back down. We need someone who will stand up to the corrupt Harrisburg establishment, even when it’s unpopular to do so.

**That’s why I entered this race, and that’s why I am asking for your vote today!**
---
[|
---](https://meyersforpa.us10.list-manage.com/track/click?u=05b9b4d233d78cbe1792acec2&id=3a8dc488fe&e=25a0acead0)
| | **I am a United States Army veteran who served eight years defending this country. I came home to Northeastern Pennsylvania and saw our freedoms under attack.

** ❌ Taxes and fees keep rising while working families get squeezed.

❌ Our Second Amendment rights face constant threats.

❌ Radical ideologies push into our schools.

❌ People don’t trust our electoral process.

❌ The unborn do not get the protection they deserve.

**Lisa Baker has enabled all of it by aligning with Harrisburg insiders rather than advocating for us. I will not do that.**

I will cut taxes and eliminate red tape so our farms and small businesses can thrive. I will defend our gun rights without compromise.

I will combat radical left-wing agendas and keep them out of our classrooms.

I will ensure secure elections with voter ID.

I will protect the unborn and stand strong for life.

**This is a fight to take Pennsylvania back and give Senate District 20 the real conservative representation it deserves.**

Today is our chance to replace the sellouts with someone who will put Pennsylvania first.

Polls close at 8:00 PM tonight. Bring your friends, family, and neighbors, and let’s make today the day we turn things around and take Pennsylvania back!

[CLICK HERE](https://meyersforpa.us10.list-manage.com/track/click?u=05b9b4d233d78cbe1792acec2&id=4dbe35cd33&e=25a0acead0) to find your polling place and make a plan to get out and vote today!

**Please feel free to contact me on my personal cell at (570) 266-1998 if you have any questions or need help locating your polling place.**

LET’S WIN!

For Pennsylvania,

## Cornyn, Paxton Hit Campaign Trail
Sen. John Cornyn and Attorney General Ken Paxton hit the campaign trail yesterday--the first day of early voting for the GOP Senate runoff next Tuesday--to [rally](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGurCAYhJ9GO83_I6gUFLex29ve0iDgwj0IBv9d17c_8bzCmWqSSWYy37_H_NAhhvT8qzen6LPmObnziI7IlXl5xViCDelpvN72LRwmJ_syNDNgfQOiQTlbHeI189qqBazE2ikcBonjKFDUXgEbR4aGd8CcdHbl68CN0BKlGBYmsA7qLgOBEhFQdC3IoVsA114CsIX3FQdnA-XSknfkPvpY45XfrrQmb3VUnmg_qu5PxaaKTed5tpf2Od9pxab7TsUmXSiY6G77P_vUmFzSlZovl5pdfyinxgdqEG71o2g9bbEuyu5niDEc_VBxeG46xJ9R-h2qt2LfAQAA___ciHyg) supporters and appeal to undecided voters. Cornyn attended events in San Antonio and Austin, while Paxton visited Dallas and Tyler. A new [poll](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGupDAQRE9jMo9sgw0EBJuQ_U03RG27GaxtbGR6PjO3X_GvsNmTSnqqqj9fyxckSvn5G3ac-L2WJeN1EjJjXfyLqKaY8jNssB97OkPJ8RV4Mco4qazU4xIh0Wfpmjh5FUfd4KT7ftTDYLVttglXjS2E1vrYjwja9ti2djAKVte7dWjSdMuU1aPWStv2oca-9UqvblTK-M6JTmFMXOqDN2R8w7nSp3xjfYSyNzRtzMcp2l_CzMLM13U9_m7ldYfCzFA5BUJh5nuXMPNRKHEKNyJh4FTyzT9eeWIGRnkUIhlKzZ8sD3hzyZKBoKZQhJnNYKW1HtA7L6NXSnatDhK6YZU-Qg8OvItdaOoUjysRpdP1olPPHRL9dOb_e_p7Mv8CAAD__wsokqk) from Texas Southern University shows both candidates are in a neck-and-neck race with Democratic state Rep. James Talarico for the general election matchup, with Cornyn leading 45% to 44% and Paxton tied at 45%. Cornyn has argued he would have the edge over Talarico in November, [citing](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDFuhDAURE8DHcjfYMCFizR0mzYlss0HOzE2Mn-X5fYRuUK6kUaa0Xtfj-mhffBx_dQbKnovaYp4HgGJME_mGUL2s4-rdXrbN3_YFOenpYkz3lVMVCCnWftwTW05K8NmCSUq6HsJwyBAlE6BhVajacRipO0Hzg20jJllaQ1q0enSq3uMCZAADERTM9k3hsHSSca4abuiZTh7Srkmh4RvfSzhSi_MtU1bGZQj2o-i-Sj4WPDxPM_60i6luy34eOMUfNSZvA14x-_kYmVTjlesSOcV6ah-MFa7flOKFUjRccYHWTvaQpnVvJ8-BH90fdGyddM-_B3T_3S9FP8NAAD__xNdf3M) infidelity allegations from Paxton's pending divorce, along with past indictments and impeachment proceedings. Paxton, meanwhile, [claims](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLuypCAQhp8Gs56CHvESGGxCdjbd0EJolVoEC9rjzNtvzXmFzf_r9-dr_rIhhrT9tgdN_FrznOiukZipzMsVYwk-pM3t9jiPUF1O_nI8o8QOpAY1zt6G-J7bxk-L9KNqaFJ9P6ph0Eo3-6QU-W5d9TIoNQyoFin98kQ96L5DiW0Tpk-Y1GpUSir9fMixfy5Srd0oJS5tJ1pJPnAuD96J6WXrGt_5m8rD5aOJ0858VvH8JdAINPd9P1wM7i_u-aqc00cl0HxuCTQ_foHm0ynQSC3QqFagcbmkdwKbPJz2xTnBcpU3kHU7ZN6pQEiQaLMcvgmsr2ArVEqWCbZ8QrlSXlegxFQqrCHZCJULsdsFmqZM_rxDjKF2vWjldtgQf_bz_1H_nvBfAAAA__-T9JcT) he would be more effective in getting Republican voters to the polls. Cornyn's campaign has spent $18 million in advertising--more than triple the amount Paxton and his allies have spent. President Trump, who [promised](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL3OpCAYha8GOwy8in4UFDZ2s-2WBgHHd8OPARxn7n7j3MLXneQk5-f5-1geGj3G5x8dnKrvLS3RXcW7Wl1e1tP7jBbj0-w6HAGLSdGepi7AYKBMUC4Xq9F_lr6xamVW8sYpPo6S__wILppdwWq5NoMEptdxFOB6IRlokHozRjDboLrDmOCSc8ZF1zI5divj2yAZg7UfSM-cxZpyW3dX3VuXzX_Sy-XWpNB4tdd6FNJNBGYC83VdbSjx9gjMLtKzEJjvUwTmI3msaG5pUo6fSI3XGAqt-QwHvVKklbpoUy6OYqTfNlpc1NXRfMa0bQRmnek0QXexf1OTlT0u9B7LMJKePYNG_91Vf0fzpeB_AAAA___-7Iqb) an endorsement the day after the March 3 primary, has yet to weigh in on the race.
## Three Teenagers Arrested in Austin Shooting Spree
Three teenage suspects tied to a [dozen shootings](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2ypCAUhVeDGV2AqE1AMInZm3RCC-G23BoEC67P7t1P-bYw8Xfq_P35Wr4cJszbb7eDpferLBmuloAI6rKeKVUMmDcf3X7s2HzJ4fS0KKFGLgYuzRIcps-iu2BXEYzswMppMvL5HOTQRet6CAM8jVZqktqM-uX7J5hV6Wmdbj3a20wM0kgp5NA_hJn6VcjXaIRQqx6ZFhCQSn1QBIK3a6_0Kd9QH77sXbKR6Gis_8XUzNR8Xdfj79vlGzI132uYmn3FHZia3RG44u1sB3hqHDP3Z6MSPtzlQhEqd8STqxv8sJIzeMKS-YUUuRS8lZMid2cjzLzFUgjzdid01YbjwpSwjRPTYtsdpp-G9H-_flv1LwAA__9boo6w) and four vehicle thefts in and around Austin over the weekend are in custody following an hours-long manhunt Sunday. Four people were injured in the shootings, and nearly 200 officers were involved in the search. Cristian Mondragon, 17, has been [identified](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkM2upCAUhJ8Gd3QOiCgLF7Nxd2c7S8PPsT25CB3A9vbbT5xXmGWlkkp935-v9ctSpPT8bQ-c28-W14RXjdgaltWdMRYKlJ5-t8froOpzCqdvqwSpOQxcmDVYip9VdWF2EIzocBbjaMQ0DWLo9hltP42jEnYDp3Cz0-BHCD1o6yaDxnU032MwCCMEiKF_gBl7B2LTBkA6pZkCDNRyebQdG_7YusVPfmN5-Hx0cd5be1XW_2JyYXK5ruvx_T7xLplcbGnkIzK53FxMLr7QcUd71kaJ17O-0DdOiV-I35gCLzaFfPC659woPSungKnRRhiYXKQ2HH3QMoDmuIHiavSSu8kq7vyktN-EspPuyhxeF8VIVY9MwfOwFP89bv_n-T3LvwEAAP__3EKRjg) as one of the suspects. The identities of the other suspects, ages 15 and 16, have not been publicly disclosed. Mondragon was recently charged with stealing a gun from Central Texas Gun Works, and the 15-year-old suspect allegedly stole a firearm from the store on Saturday. Later that day and the next, gunfire was [reported](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuhDAQRL8GOtCuwYALF2noLm1KZPByrGQwwstx9_cR-YV0I400o_d-HsPDceDt-e1WsvKe47DRlQKJ0DGMZwgHe96e0-LWfeU0xc2fkwwKVFOALtAM3nH4DHXu7QjeYE4W29Zg12nU-WJNW8HsZzV2tXdj1zjy4FpCrbWqG3Q523sMNBpEQF2VYNpqBJwbA6DGuslqIM8Sj1IWEnq7NIdPfNFRTnHNg11E9pRVX5nqM9Vf11V-3BLj3Waqv3Ey1btDeAp0R2yLGHyRzrTTJAV72oRnJl-4MwlvBTZagda6LhdZQ35Yv18cAqemzWp4ro7D37X8T9jLqt8AAAD__3-df1c) at several locations in South and East Austin. Mondragon and the 15-year-old suspect were arrested Sunday afternoon in Manor following a police pursuit, and the third suspect was [arrested](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkM-uojAcRp8GdpK20CKLLgZHFs5gxoVxZjak_5CfFkposXqf_sb7Cnf1bb6cnJxL27UCLEzXoxgND8_edZOJ3poQzNLJ1doFNExXNYhxHsErN-lVhY4gwjaIbnDVaQH21RWp5hLpCqeG47Ks8HZLMU0HXm0VoRJj2hPJJMlzJJVGuSyJNoRpkQJ_wxDFFcYI0zxDVZlLhHtWIURkwZICGQ3BLVkYTDBP4Xv7cg-zZMqNqeVDCLNP8h8JaRLSxBizXigjnbu_DwlpWjG55Y-zoExCmtn54N_bS9Aop78P9HTW9LA73XbAaigk07djvT_8_7gPsjUwXMSt9u3-nwrrz1jG8dczxPq8u8_79W9v04XrOYK14FmZFOg6CrBfauF7QR-cfAYAAP__-YaK3Q) hours later. Police issued shelter-in-place orders for parts of Austin and Manor as they investigated the shootings and searched for the suspects. Police haven't disclosed a motive for the violence, which they described as "a mix of random and targeted shootings." Yesterday, Gov. | | | | Dear Fellow Arizonan,
May is Jewish American Heritage Month, a time to celebrate the extraordinary contributions Jewish Americans have made to our country and the values that have helped shape the American story. From science and medicine to education, business, public service, and the arts, Jewish culture and leadership are deeply woven into the fabric of our nation.
Jewish American Heritage Month is also a reminder that people of conscience must never stay silent in the face of antisemitism.
Across America, we are seeing a disturbing rise in antisemitism and extremist rhetoric. Hyper-partisan voices are increasingly tolerating and amplifying anti-American and Islamist ideology that is, [as I have said many times before](https://b9jvufebb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001TqPTVAtMwYaZkOmFkkuhQ2XBk2SUxTndrQtVULbbwILMDoBiTtVdfN2umgbfAud7uZsn_A0Co-Adgb45g6rkWLj81cwcz6tKyYU2BbYnjloJPGgmAWvdzpORuIpNEt8pG7kLCrjm9yDyYaKmV8hxpi75LfCI_S7WdJltzQsCmyWyCB6kvSA69g==&c=-lG9ddOh1h25z2nIIQwst7gWuiS4JAVK85x4rSsz3lhqgCo7IEP82g==&ch=ptrql6QeADHJsX5Ks837ssvq7KUSSnFIiYADICEMBBKx0cicXdvJtA==), fundamentally incompatible with Western culture, individual liberty, and the American way of life.
As a Muslim, Navy veteran, physician, and reformer who has spent decades standing up to extremism within my own faith, I believe silence is not an option. Supporting the Jewish community and defending Israel is not only in America's strategic interest, but it is also central to who we are as Americans.
I have spent my life defending American values and standing up to extremism because America is worth defending for generations to come.
Meanwhile, Greg Stanton has stayed silent as antisemitic rhetoric and radical ideology continue spreading within his own party, falling in line with the same hyper-partisan political movement that has normalized hostility toward Israel and appeased dangerous anti-American voices like Hasan Piker, who are working to radicalize our youth.
Arizona's 4th Congressional District deserves an independent voice in Congress willing to confront extremism, defend our ally Israel, and stand up for American values.
That is exactly what I intend to do.

The United States Senate confirmed Andrew B. | | Hey folks, Dennis Quaid here.

Here’s the thing: life doesn’t come with guarantees. The economy shifts, markets stumble, and years of hard work could slip through your fingers like sand.

Should it happen again—what’s your plan?

Think back just a few years. Inflation wasn’t the monster it feels like today. Prices made sense. The future felt steady.

But today? It’s a different story. Groceries cost more. Gas went up. And rising costs chip away at the value of your retirement savings every day.

But you don’t have to sit on the sidelines:
You’ve seen what happens when folks don’t prepare. It gets ugly. Savings accounts drain faster than expected, plans get downgraded, and peace of mind turns to heart-racing anxiety.

Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | Market Commentary Disclaimer We encourage all readers to consult a qualified financial professional — such as a registered investment adviser or licensed broker — before making any investment decision. ---
For years, the Left thought they had a permanent grip on America's youth.

And honestly?

For a while, they did.
They dominated classrooms. Social media. Pop culture. Hollywood. Universities.

They told an entire generation that loving your country was shameful...

That faith was outdated... And traditional values were something to erase.

But thanks to Charlie's leadership, something incredible has happened:

Young men are rejecting the Left in RECORD numbers. High school boys are the most Conservative they've been in 50 years.

And Gen Z is heading back to church -- in numbers greater than their parents' or grandparents' generations.

For the first time in decades, we are WINNING the American Culture War.

**But there 's still one group the Left is desperately fighting to hold onto: **

_America 's young women. _

Because they know something very important, Peter...

If they can win the hearts and minds of young women...

They don't just shape individuals. They shape families. They shape homes. They shape future generations.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
---
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Joining Steve is Peter Francis Dante an American character actor, comedian and singer. He appeared in sixteen films from Happy Madison Productions, often alongside Adam Sandler. Dante's roles are usually alongside Jonathan Loughran and/or Allen Covert. He played Peter in Little Nicky. In Grandma's Boy he played Dante. He played a lawyer named Tommy in Adam Sandler's movie Big Daddy. He played the quarterback Gee Grenouille in The Waterboy and Murph "Murphy" in Mr. Deeds. He played a security guard in 50 First Dates. For more about Peter visit [https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0200601/](https://substack.com/redirect/9a256b92-4e40-43c6-bd5c-640e8c21b3fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

body:
Following SCOTUS gerrymandering catastrophe, some analysts now forecast a real chance of outright defeat for the Democratic Party this midterm election.
| | | | | [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001HX_zZsrrN3SEd1J1OyQkCjB2T1NDimI5049FPcPP8ZyQSmuI6KcM04Fc2iNNfAUA8WGe66-4P-H6FUW1JSgcnOaKO2gB1i_kwfhKVevOs_QCx_EZDNAbbtUfndgBjbQHzrny3Ki_bw8tEhphhqi_KipvSiAFuj5DQk4CjegKJSKKXSxemKKnTvNF5dsv8pYoK3g0aJ4BempWZvElELr8rb6my3f4euYl&c=-85oAEteiRw6mQaYaZBOBGBSDiO0LjlxILRM5RUk4lH849IQbsDMvg==&ch=9RZBaxR-3FaTA1KpR6s14lTm04Pj-PGOBAqktaGghWVNiHkMAgnm3Q==)

| Peter,
Following the Supreme Court's gerrymandering catastrophe, analysts now forecast a real chance of outright defeat for the Democratic Party this midterm election.
Our survival now rides on the forlorn hope of 19 Black Dems, now in red seats, winning tough races.
This is Congressman Cleo Fields (D-LA) - and up until this past Thursday, I represented a deep blue district. Then, at 4:30 in the morning, MAGA lawmakers quietly redrew my district and made it deep red.
Analysts say the odds are stacked against us. But as a man of faith, I also believe in miracles.
---
| [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001HX_zZsrrN3SEd1J1OyQkCjB2T1NDimI5049FPcPP8ZyQSmuI6KcM04Fc2iNNfAUA8WGe66-4P-H6FUW1JSgcnOaKO2gB1i_kwfhKVevOs_QCx_EZDNAbbtUfndgBjbQHzrny3Ki_bw8tEhphhqi_KipvSiAFuj5DQk4CjegKJSKKXSxemKKnTvNF5dsv8pYoK3g0aJ4BempWZvElELr8rbtURXVb0qrO&c=-85oAEteiRw6mQaYaZBOBGBSDiO0LjlxILRM5RUk4lH849IQbsDMvg==&ch=9RZBaxR-3FaTA1KpR6s14lTm04Pj-PGOBAqktaGghWVNiHkMAgnm3Q==)

The victories of the Civil Rights era were miracles. Scripture also reminds us that faith without works is dead. All of those victories were built through sacrifice, organizing, and action.
I need you to do more than believe in me, or to believe that change will eventually come. Between now and July, we must build the resources necessary to compete and prove these pundits wrong.
Louisiana can't fund this fight alone. We need help. Most of the support we need will have to come from people across the country who understand what's at stake and want to get involved how they can.

name: Elissa Slotkin
subject: I know... I know...
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ELISSA SLOTKIN FOR MICHIGAN
body:
I acknowledge there's a very good chance you didn't wake up and think "I am going to make a contribution to Elissa Slotkin today. I get it.

| | | | | | | | | | |
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---
Good morning. It's Elissa Slotkin.

I acknowledge there's a very good chance you didn't wake up and think "I am going to make a contribution to Elissa Slotkin today." I get it.

But that is what I am asking you to do.

I am one of a small number of Democratic Senators who won their race at the same time Donald Trump won that state.

Over the next few months, I am going to travel a bit and help Democrats in tough races -- like I've done for a number of candidates and in a number of "red" states already. But we're just getting started.

Here in Michigan, we also have an open Senate seat, a governor's race and a number of other close races. I know how to find voters in so-called "red' areas and can help make the difference -- something that will be important after some tough primaries.

[**If making sure Democrats have a chance of retaking the Senate, the House and supporting candidates in tough races is important to you, I am asking you to make a contribution before our May fundraising drive ends in a few days to help make that happen.**](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/3865?refcode=em260521&t=1&akid=2454%2E135344%2E03RLzp)

Thank you. - Elissa Elissa Slotkin |

My name is Marialana Kinter and I'm running for Congress in District 7 because I believe it's time to take power out of the hands of corporate PACs and put it back in the hands of the people. Running against Corey Mills, I am refusing corporate PAC money because our government should work for everyday people, not special interests. I'm fighting to overturn Citizens United, protect voting rights, strengthen ethics laws, ban congressional stock trading, increase transparency in campaign finance, and make Congress more accountable to working families across District 7 and the country. ### Virtual Townhall- Redistricting & Voting Rights
Between gerrymandered maps and the narrowing of the Voting Rights Act, the voices of working families are being systematically silenced by politicians looking for self-gain. Join Marialana Kinter and a panel of Congressional candidates from across the state for a critical conversation on the state of our democracy and the path forward to ensure every Floridian has fair and equal representation. This is a conversation led by our community. We will talk about how changing voting maps affects our neighborhoods and how we can protect the voices of every group. We will also discuss the laws we need to pass, such as the John Lewis Voting Rights Act, to make sure everyone in Florida is represented fairly. Our Panelists:
* Marialana Kinter (FL-07)
* Bernard Taylor (FL-21)
* Mark David (FL-16)
* Ron Merchinson (FL-06)
* Eric Yonce (FL-06)
