### Weekly Volunteer Virtual Meetings

Join Team Kinter and help us build a people-powered movement for Florida's 7th Congressional District. Marialana Kinter is fighting for working families, affordable living, and a government that puts people before corporate interests. We need volunteers like you to help make it happen. We're inviting supporters to sign up for our weekly volunteer meetings, where you can learn how to get involved through canvassing, phone banking, community outreach, digital organizing, and more. This week, our volunteer meeting time has been moved up to 6:00 PM instead of 7:00 PM. We also now have new volunteer committees so supporters can plug in where their skills and passions fit best. Our committees include Press and Media, Data and Precinct Captains, Administrative and Research, Events, and Tabling. When you sign up, you can share your availability, skills, and the ways you'd like to support the campaign. You can also request a campaign shirt and get connected with the volunteer opportunities that best fit you.

clean_body: Join Team Kinter upcoming events! | | | | | == | | Marialana Kinter is Ready to Fight for Your Rights This Is Why Our Campaign Refuses Corporate PAC Money! | | == | == My name is Marialana Kinter and I'm running for Congress in District 7 because I believe it's time to take power out of the hands of corporate PACs and put it back in the hands of the people. Running against Corey Mills, I am refusing corporate PAC money because our government should work for everyday people, not special interests. I'm fighting to overturn Citizens United, protect voting rights, strengthen ethics laws, ban congressional stock trading, increase transparency in campaign finance, and make Congress more accountable to working families across District 7 and the country. I hope you'll get involved and learn more about my priorities at == | Upcoming Events | | == | == Virtual Townhall- Redistricting & Voting Rights Between gerrymandered maps and the narrowing of the Voting Rights Act, the voices of working families are being systematically silenced by politicians looking for self-gain. Join Marialana Kinter and a panel of Congressional candidates from across the state for a critical conversation on the state of our democracy and the path forward to ensure every Floridian has fair and equal representation. This is a conversation led by our community. We will talk about how changing voting maps affects our neighborhoods and how we can protect the voices of every group. We will also discuss the laws we need to pass, such as the John Lewis Voting Rights Act, to make sure everyone in Florida is represented fairly. Our Panelists: Marialana Kinter (FL-07) Bernard Taylor (FL-21) Mark David (FL-16) Ron Merchinson (FL-06) Eric Yonce (FL-06) | | == | == Democratic Progressive Caucus Canvass with Angie Nixon and Marialana Kinter The only way we win this race is by talking directly to our neighbors. We are united by the belief that we deserve better and we can have it. That change starts with us--mobilizing together and reaching our neighbors directly to build the community we all deserve Join Marialana and the team this Saturday as we hit the pavement in Casselberry to discuss our mission to stop the squeeze on working families, protect our environment, and bring real accountability to Washington. Whether you are a seasoned canvasser or this is your first time, we have a spot for you! We will provide training, scripts, and walk lists. Bring comfortable shoes, a water bottle, and your Kinter for Congress gear! Mission Details: Meetup Time: 9:50 AM (For training and materials) Canvassing Hours: 10:00 AM - 12:00 PM Location: 419 Forest Park Lane - Casselberry, FL, USA | | == | == Meet & Greet with Marialana Kinter! Join us after our Saturday canvass for a special Meet and Greet with Marialana Kinter, congressional candidate for Florida's 7th Congressional District. This is a great opportunity to connect directly with Marialana, hear more about her vision for CD7, and ask questions about the race and the issues impacting our communities. Light bites will be available, and we encourage everyone to bring a friend. Even if you cannot participate in the canvass earlier in the day, we would still love for you to come meet Marialana and spend time with fellow supporters and community members. Join us on Saturday, May 23rd at 1:30 PM at 480 S Ronald Reagan Blvd, Longwood, FL 32750. | | == | == Weekly Volunteer Virtual Meetings Join Team Kinter and help us build a people-powered movement for Florida's 7th Congressional District. Marialana Kinter is fighting for working families, affordable living, and a government that puts people before corporate interests. We need volunteers like you to help make it happen. We're inviting supporters to sign up for our weekly volunteer meetings, where you can learn how to get involved through canvassing, phone banking, community outreach, digital organizing, and more. This week, our volunteer meeting time has been moved up to 6:00 PM instead of 7:00 PM. We also now have new volunteer committees so supporters can plug in where their skills and passions fit best. Our committees include Press and Media, Data and Precinct Captains, Administrative and Research, Events, and Tabling. When you sign up, you can share your availability, skills, and the ways you'd like to support the campaign. You can also request a campaign shirt and get connected with the volunteer opportunities that best fit you. Wednesday, May 20th at 6 PM * Please take a few minutes to fill out the form and become part of the movement for real change in District 7. If you have any questions, contact us at mailto:lee@kinterforcongress.com. | | | == | | == | | == | | | | | | | == | Paid For By Marialana Kinter for Congress | P.O.Box 620511 | Oviedo, FL 32762 US | | | | | | |

Peter, What Tennessee just did is a throwback to one of the ugliest chapters in American history. Just hours after the Supreme Court gutted Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, the state put its plan into motion. And eight days later, they had a new congressional map. Republicans in the state had erased Tennessee’s only Black opportunity district — creating a map in which all nine of the state’s districts were majority-white. Their actions directly aim to prevent the people of Memphis — one of the largest U.S. cities with a majority Black population — from being able to elect a representative of their choice. **Tennessee Republicans are not alone. ** **Louisiana** suspended an ongoing election to rip up their current map and eliminate a Black opportunity district. **Alabama, Mississippi, and South Carolina** are all making moves to follow in their footsteps. If there was any doubt that the protections of the Voting Rights Act are still essential today, the rushed actions of these southern states should put that to rest. **The Republican Party is waging an active campaign to reboot Jim Crow. ** It is brazen, it is shameless, it is wrong — and it must fail. History is playing out in front of our eyes, and it requires us to muster every ounce of energy we have to fight back. # Raising Brave Girls in Today’s Culture
---
| |
---
| | For more than a decade, Patti Garibay poured herself into the Girl Scouts. She led troops, invested in young girls, and believed in the mission of building the next generation of strong, capable women. But over time, she watched something shift — the biblical values that had once anchored the organization began to quietly disappear, replaced by an ideology she could no longer stand behind. So she did something remarkable. She didn't just leave. She built something better. That decision became American Heritage Girls — a God-centered scouting program dedicated to raising young women of integrity through faith, service, and adventure. What started as one leader's conviction has grown into a nationwide movement, offering girls a place where their faith isn't just tolerated, but celebrated. That story deserves to be heard — listen to the full episode on [YouTube](https://momsforamerica.us/so/80PuiA59z/c?w=lF0LIiTTnCSKKUeYOojt4c7XcAw-rd9dxNtVc8CDxCk.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cueW91dHViZS5jb20vQE1vbXNmb3JBbWVyaWNhIiwiciI6IjgyNjUyOGI3LTE0YjEtNDRkYS05YWZiLWI5ZDJmYzhkOTE5YiIsIm0iOiJtYWlsIiwiYyI6IjRhYTNmYzQzLWRiNWUtNDE2Ni05YmMyLWQ3ZGZiNzJkNzIxNCJ9), [Rumble](https://momsforamerica.us/so/80PuiA59z/c?w=n1OwCsh8NfrZgKWGv04epxFm82VqFDzjzf4NzXwwZGM.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9ydW1ibGUuY29tL2MvYy0xMjA2NzMzP2U5cz1zcmNfdjFfY2JsIiwiciI6IjgyNjUyOGI3LTE0YjEtNDRkYS05YWZiLWI5ZDJmYzhkOTE5YiIsIm0iOiJtYWlsIiwiYyI6IjRhYTNmYzQzLWRiNWUtNDE2Ni05YmMyLWQ3ZGZiNzJkNzIxNCJ9), [Spotify](https://momsforamerica.us/so/80PuiA59z/c?w=XpE7WZltAVgUwhZoxiWnTjUKqW5nbX_Fuzt40W3KSMA.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9vcGVuLnNwb3RpZnkuY29tL3Nob3cvMHBIemFBWGJCRVVFUlBxajluQlhxYyIsInIiOiI4MjY1MjhiNy0xNGIxLTQ0ZGEtOWFmYi1iOWQyZmM4ZDkxOWIiLCJtIjoibWFpbCIsImMiOiI0YWEzZmM0My1kYjVlLTQxNjYtOWJjMi1kN2RmYjcyZDcyMTQifQ) or [Apple](https://momsforamerica.us/so/80PuiA59z/c?w=JoKDI54MpybVZUdfCbApzUXR9jQid5mkH3Q3tk4Jf8Y.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9wb2RjYXN0cy5hcHBsZS5jb20vdXMvcG9kY2FzdC9tb21zLWZvci1hbWVyaWNhLXBvZGNhc3QvaWQxNjE2OTIwMTIxIiwiciI6IjgyNjUyOGI3LTE0YjEtNDRkYS05YWZiLWI5ZDJmYzhkOTE5YiIsIm0iOiJtYWlsIiwiYyI6IjRhYTNmYzQzLWRiNWUtNDE2Ni05YmMyLWQ3ZGZiNzJkNzIxNCJ9) and share it with every mom who needs to hear it.

### Tips to Raise Girls Who are Strong, Courageous, and Kind
---
| |
---
| | Parenting boys or girls has some new and prevalent challenges in this generation. They are digital natives growing up in a world with endless screens, instant information, and gratification, and artificial intelligence that puts a spin on everything they read or view. They will have peers who are being raised believing that gender is fluid and that families can have two moms – two dads – or, perhaps, an even stranger scenario, like the "throuple" in Canada raising a baby together. I'm speechless on that one. Thankfully, your girls have you. You are the one who will make all the difference in their young lives from infancy to adulthood and everything in between. We also want to tip our hat to those raising girls who came from the foster care system into your home – and maybe your relationship began when they were 2, or 6, or 14. Moms are heroes, and you are pivotal to your daughter's future. That's why we are sharing a few tips for raising girls who are strong, courageous, and kind. | Peter,
While Louisiana families struggle with skyrocketing inflation from Trump's disastrous Iran War, while farmers face a fertilizer shortage and diesel price hike threatening their livelihoods, Governor Jeff Landry hopped on a plane to lead Trump's "special envoy" to Greenland. Yes. Greenland.

The same governor who just suspended an ongoing election to gut Black voter representation. The same governor who's been doing Trump's dirty work in Louisiana while his constituents suffer. He left the state to help Trump's imperialist ambitions. So much for "America First."
But here's what happened while Landry was packing his suitcase for Greenland: there was a massive backlash against MAGA at the polls. On Saturday, Democrat and Black voter turnout surged. Current MAGA Senator Bill Cassidy became the first incumbent senator to lose a primary in over a decade. And all five constitutional amendments endorsed by Governor Landry? Shot down. Every single one.
The backlash is real. The blue wave is building. And we're not waiting around to see what happens next -- we're building Organize Louisiana, an unprecedented turnout operation to power the comeback. Saturday was proof our plan is working. We just need the fuel to keep building:

# **Six states hold pivotal Tuesday primaries testing Trump 's GOP dominance in most expensive House race ever**
Voters in Alabama, Georgia, Idaho, Kentucky, Oregon and Pennsylvania vote Tuesday in U.S. House, Senate and gubernatorial primaries as Republicans defend slim majorities, with **[President Donald Trump targeting Rep. Thomas Massie](https://substack.com/redirect/cd3db180-1b2e-46e9-9b31-35c4a894288c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as MAGA enemy number one.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/cd3db180-1b2e-46e9-9b31-35c4a894288c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **The Massie race:** The Kentucky 4th District race between libertarian-minded Massie--a Trump critic over Iran war policy and unconditional Israel aid who pushed for Epstein files release--and Trump-backed former Navy SEAL Ed Gallrein has become the most expensive House primary in history with $32+ million spent, much from Trump allies and pro-Israel groups, with War Secretary Pete Hegseth campaigning for Gallrein on primary eve.
* **Massie says Trump attacks may backfire, defends foreign policy stance** : The 14-year congressman **[told Fox News Digital](https://substack.com/redirect/cd3db180-1b2e-46e9-9b31-35c4a894288c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that Trump's social media taunts show "he's losing sleep, his reputation is on the line. He really shouldn't have got involved in this race," defending his opposition to all foreign aid by saying "When I said America First, I meant it. I don't vote for foreign aid to Egypt, to Syria, to Ukraine...and I'm not going to ruin it by sending foreign aid to one country."
* **Georgia gubernatorial and Senate races test Trump endorsement power, Kentucky Senate primary features McConnell successor battle** : Trump backs Georgia Lt. Gov. Burt Jones for governor against billionaire Rick Jackson who's spent $80+ million. In Kentucky's Senate race to succeed retiring Mitch McConnell, Trump-endorsed Rep. Andy Barr faces former Attorney General Daniel Cameron among 11 GOP candidates.

| Folks, I didn’t make this decision lightly.

When I announced my campaign for governor of Wisconsin, I did it because I saw how much our working families were struggling – and what would be at stake if a Republican was elected to lead this state.

_Healthcare costs are skyrocketing because Tom Tiffany voted against extending subsidies.

Our family farms and small businesses are feeling the squeeze due to the Trump-Tiffany economic plan.

And when Republicans care more about lining the pockets of their billionaire backers, working families lose out on affordable housing and groceries._

**I’m in this race for the same reason I first began public service — because Wisconsinites deserve a state where they can thrive, not just scrape by paycheck to paycheck.[**_In a few hours, we’re closing the books on our $13,000 daily fundraising goal. If you agree with me, you can use this link to make a contribution of any amount to power our campaign. →_**](https://act.mandelabarnes.com/go/7008?refcode=LOC_EM_FR_2026.05.19_EOM_B1_F1_S1_C1_30DO30DC_RS-T0&t=5&akid=6187%2E196590%2EzrOCfG)** | | [ CHIP IN NOW → ](https://act.mandelabarnes.com/go/7008?refcode=LOC_EM_FR_2026.05.19_EOM_B1_F1_S1_C1_30DO30DC_RS-T0&t=6&akid=6187%2E196590%2EzrOCfG)

**Tom Tiffany will bring the rampant dysfunction and far-right extremism of Washington here to Wisconsin.**

Thanks to grassroots supporters like you, we’ve built a movement that is ready to do things the Wisconsin Way, not the Washington Way.

That means finally expanding healthcare, delivering relief for our farmers and small businesses, lowering the cost of housing, and raising wages.

This is the kind of bold vision we deserve — and it will take all of us coming together to achieve it. [](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260519-1.cUhSE1&amount=5&refcode=em20260519-654&t=1&akid=654%2E34582%2EL-RdIe)
When I taught at Mankato West High School in the late 1990s, I started out coaching linebackers and then became defensive coordinator for the varsity football team.
The Scarlets had a couple of rough seasons before I got there, losing 27 straight games. Whether it's football games or political races, it can feel impossible or hopeless to come out of that kind of loss.
In 1999, even though we started with a disappointing 2-4 record, I made it a point to tell my players: _the season was far from over._
We rolled up our sleeves and went after it, working hard to get better and better. After winning 8 consecutive games, the team went on to become state champions, winning the 1999 Minnesota AAAA Prep Bowl in a 35-28 game.
**It goes to show that when we inspire our kids to dream, set lofty goals, and lift each other up to achieve them,_we win._**
It’s the same approach I’ve used as governor, and it’s the attitude I have now as we set out to recruit and elect a new generation of Democrats to represent small towns across the country. I’m talking about folks who are everyday leaders in their communities: teachers, farmers, nurses, veterans, and more.
We need more candidates who can speak to regular Americans, not just DC consultants, and who share the lived experience of raising a family and trying to get by in the places often written off by corporations and the billionaire class.
But to find and support them, it’s going to take a lot of folks like you pitching in $5 or $10 here and there to build up our resources, especially in these first few months as we get Small Town PAC off the ground heading into the 2026 midterms.
[**So Peter, can I count on you to chip in whatever you can to Small Town PAC today to help Democrats compete and WIN in more places across the country this November and beyond?**](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260519-1.cUhSE1&amount=5&refcode=em20260519-654&t=2&akid=654%2E34582%2EL-RdIe)

Clear eyes, full hearts, can’t lose.
— Tim

Tim Walz started Small Town PAC to build a Democratic Party that invests in small towns and delivers a message that resonates with rural America.
Together, we're finding and recruiting thoughtful, hardworking people to run for office, and supporting a new generation of leaders who truly reflect and understand their communities.
**[It’s time for Democrats to expand the map and put small towns back at the forefront: pitch in now to help build our movement from the ground up.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/stp-ms-em-footer?refcode=em20260519-654&t=22&refcode2=654_34582_L-RdIe&akid=654%2E34582%2EL-RdIe)**

name: Douglas Carswell
subject: Raise the Flag!
body:
| | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/mspolicy/usnationaldebt-12853351?e=5703353baa)
---
| |
---
| Dear Friend,
I rarely ask favors, but here's one worth a minute of your time — and it costs you nothing.

Thanks to a bill passed in the 2025 Mississippi Legislative Session (good job Rep Trey Lamar!), our state has authorized its first-ever Gadsden Flag specialty license tag. "Don't Tread on Me" — on Mississippi plates, rolling down Mississippi roads. I love the idea.
---
|
---
| But there's a catch. The State won't start producing the tags until 300 Mississippians have registered for one. The folks running this effort have been working at it all semester and have come within striking distance — they're just **14 registrations short**.

That's where you come in.

The first 300 tags are **free**. All you have to do is fill out the short form at [**gadsdentag.com**](https://us.list-manage.com/18AqZz86AMF?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3). After the first 300 free tags are claimed, the tag will be available for purchase at your local county tax assessor's office — but why pay if you can get one free and help push this across the finish line?

If you've ever wanted a small, daily way to fly the flag for liberty in Mississippi, this is it. Please take 60 seconds to register, and forward this email to a friend or two who would love one of these on their truck.

A free Gadsden tag, a stronger statement for freedom on Mississippi roads, and 14 more registrations is all it takes.
---
| [Register Here!](https://us.list-manage.com/3ued7qqo1AZ?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3 "Register Here!")

---
For liberty,

Douglas Carswell

Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
How did Americans across the country, especially in the South, respond to the Supreme Court's decision to legally codify racial gerrymandering? They turned out in droves to march for their fundamental right to vote, folks.
For those of us who couldn't make it to Selma, Montgomery, or other places to march? We have to do everything we can to register a tidal wave of voters across the country.
Voter registration is a critical part of grassroots efforts to protect voting rights. The more people who vote, the more our government looks like we, the people. But to get to the point where every voice is heard, we need your help .
Every $3 chipped in can help us register a new voter. If you're with us in this fight, please pitch in $30 or whatever you can today to help register 10 new voters >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?refcode=051926_1&amount=30]
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:

This was a devastating blow to voting rights, but it only serves to strengthen our resolve. If anti-voting forces are going to stack the deck against the communities we serve, then we will work even harder to engage and rally these voters, lift their voices, and defend their right to vote.
Despite vote-suppressing courts and state legislatures making it harder to register to vote -- passing bills to stop organizations like ours and our partners on the ground from helping potential voters navigate the increasingly murky rules around voter registration -- we're still pulling out all the stops to bring voters into the system.
Voter participation has been increasing. Voting quickly becomes a habit -- a habit our democracy sorely needs to fulfill the promise of the American dream. Overwhelming key states with new voter registrations can help turn the tide against the voter suppression laws we've seen passed the last few years.
This voter registration work, at just about $3 per new voter, is how we can make the greatest impact. Fuel our efforts with $30 to give us the resources we need to register new voters ahead of the 2026 deadlines >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?refcode=051926_1&amount=30]

body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/AV/AVLCV/1/70877/images/51926%20Election%20Day%20-%20email%20header.png]
Peter,
Election Day is here! That means today your superpower is making sure that your vote gets counted.
If you haven’t already returned your ballot, put yours in an official dropbox by 8pm tonight (5/19) to ensure your vote is counted. Use the dropbox locator here [https://sos.oregon.gov/voting/Pages/drop-box-locator.aspx] .
Find your Dropbox [https://sos.oregon.gov/voting/Pages/drop-box-locator.aspx]
Please note that due to federal changes at USPS, we have passed the recommended deadline to mail your ballot in. You are advised to use a dropbox instead to ensure your ballot will be counted.
As we head into what is likely to be a record hot summer, fresh off of a record dry winter, we need to elect climate champions at all levels of government. We need climate voters like you to turnout! Check out our Primary Endorsements [https://www.olcv.org/2026-primary/] here, and look at our Environmental Voter Guide [https://www.olcv.org/2026-environmental-voter-guide/] for some races we didn’t make an endorsement in. And, if you still have questions about voting, refer to our Voter Resources [https://www.olcv.org/2026-voter-resources/] or reply to this email. We are happy to help!
The clock is ticking, so drop your ballot off at a dropbox by 8pm tonight and become a superhero for our environment!
Already voted? Text 5 friends and family members a reminder to vote by 8pm today!
Thank you for using your voice for our climate.
Happy voting,
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/AV/AVLCV/1/70877/images/Britney_signature-removebg-preview.png]

subject: Your free eBook
body:
Today the American family is in crisis.

| | | [](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zbegafibh59k6d4vpvm9kp1124jna3j1dri3od7o_rp22sh2s8i6epr4s9i6eoj6c9h2bs)

| | Dear Fellow American,

Today the American family is in crisis.

The statistics are sobering. Marriage rates are near historic lows. One in three young Americans is projected never to marry. Birth rates continue to fall. These trends are not abstractions--they are warning signs.
---
|
[](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2ztf0fl0ooo1p0if5rfdij77rcm75upkrfindamg8_rp22sh2s8i6epr4s9i6eoj6c9h2bs)
---
| | We cannot let our nation reach the brink of irreversible population decline.

That is why, after years of rigorous research, The Heritage Foundation's released a groundbreaking report: **" Saving America by Saving the Family: A Foundation for the Next 250 Years." **

This new report presents practical reforms designed to help American families live the good life and make marriage and family formation more attainable for the next generation.

_Our democracy survives when people choose to protect it._
Today we are once again living through a hugely important moment in our nation’s history. The democratic values generations of Americans have fought so hard for are under attack.
**And here in New Hampshire, the stakes could not be higher.**

| | | | | [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0015813mgAsgC87xmzcvvR7uvZZLh2ad8ZuaZbHaYorFVtQwj3zNjpKtdEp6Jyatom_B2jQEJAyPnUIa-0sLWiLfXTp-A79SbYytCdqamrsNpw67HwkFrYcEf_Xt0SAp0mUcEpvDioC3iUKXyttJFWL7C21oSGB8MG8P42MIg4O5PXa2TgqnKjN_SGB3Txb5lytmBc-rWaOJmUwaJF5z53B4nVqIrNAPWns8zN95fuhx5k=&c=BHY8ZYtDDdVK367Tm7_e5rZ-NparB27HUrM5lLsstDVnMyaK12780A==&ch=vE2YaK6fkjm668btFRIPdoYZk88VSZaouF82Hn8YoQfTawzyvN9rrg==)

|
Peter,
Georgians are voting right now. Democrats are surging. And MAGA just showed you exactly what we're fighting.
Two days ago, a judicial watchdog panel made up entirely of Republican appointees accused Jen Jordan and Miracle Rankin of violating ethics rules -- for speaking about abortion rights and appearing together in a television commercial.[ ](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0015813mgAsgC87xmzcvvR7uvZZLh2ad8ZuaZbHaYorFVtQwj3zNjpKtdEp6Jyatom_rBG0WHyBOz6DNaEvH7N4UmrULGg2K9kuceFK4cItUsrRQQlr_i6e-0WNiln1mIdr9NkXTcqoYyeofgiDQWeGYW_ZrZ8pIXim5GUqQMdrHDBnsxXlK-utfyWkTtYCzNcy4dACbJ6V9R4hEwPDDzLtpQ==&c=BHY8ZYtDDdVK367Tm7_e5rZ-NparB27HUrM5lLsstDVnMyaK12780A==&ch=vE2YaK6fkjm668btFRIPdoYZk88VSZaouF82Hn8YoQfTawzyvN9rrg==)
They said "we'll fight for you." In a campaign ad. On television.
---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0015813mgAsgC87xmzcvvR7uvZZLh2ad8ZuaZbHaYorFVtQwj3zNjpKtdEp6Jyatom_B2jQEJAyPnUIa-0sLWiLfXTp-A79SbYytCdqamrsNpw67HwkFrYcEf_Xt0SAp0mUcEpvDioC3iUKXyttJFWL7C21oSGB8MG8P42MIg4O5PXa2TgqnKjN_SGB3Txb5lytmBc-rWaOJmUwaJF5z53B4jUZLGXDaCipctgdRXADQOE=&c=BHY8ZYtDDdVK367Tm7_e5rZ-NparB27HUrM5lLsstDVnMyaK12780A==&ch=vE2YaK6fkjm668btFRIPdoYZk88VSZaouF82Hn8YoQfTawzyvN9rrg==)
---
For that, a GOP-stacked panel launched an investigation, fought it to the federal appeals court, and timed the release for 48 hours before Election Day.
The Georgia Democratic Party called it "dirty work." That's exactly what it is. It's also desperate.
But that is exactly what happens when those who have taken power from the American people react when they know they are poised to lose it. And it is what we will be up against every single day -- at the state level and the federal level -- for as long as Leonard Leo's dark money machine controls our courts.
This is the stacked deck.
Eight of Georgia's nine Supreme Court justices were appointed by Republican governors. The commission that just attacked our candidates was appointed by Republicans. We love having you in our network, but if you only want our most important email updates,[click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/108?t=2&akid=2299%2E259176%2EBHv849) If you'd like to unsubscribe, [click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/109?t=3&akid=2299%2E259176%2EBHv849)_

[](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/11036?source=LOC_EM_FR_2026.05.20_Luria-Chutzpah_B2_F1_S15_C15_90AC-365DON_RS-T0&t=4&akid=2299%2E259176%2EBHv849) Peter, it’s Elaine Luria, and Blue Amp Action said I could reach out because it’s a pivotal moment for our campaign. The Virginia Supreme Court just struck down the new congressional map that Virginia voters passed last month. [**So, our race just became even more crucial to our battle for the House Majority. Before I get into my background and how I’m fighting back, will you split a $25 donation to flip VA-02?**](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/11036?source=LOC_EM_FR_2026.05.20_Luria-Chutzpah_B2_F1_S15_C15_90AC-365DON_RS-T0&t=5&akid=2299%2E259176%2EBHv849) | [DONATE $25](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/11036?source=LOC_EM_FR_2026.05.20_Luria-Chutzpah_B2_F1_S15_C15_90AC-365DON_RS-T0&t=6&akid=2299%2E259176%2EBHv849)
---
_Chutzpah_ — is a Yiddish term that means _guts_ or _courage._
In 1906, my great-grandfather left his home in Poland, made the long journey through Europe and across the Atlantic, and landed in Jasper, Alabama.
That took some serious _chutzpah._
My great-grandfather believed so strongly in the promise of America – a place where he could be Jewish without fear, where he could forge his own path – that he left his whole world behind.
That promise came true for him. He built a life, a family, and a proud community.
That’s what sets America apart, Peter. Here, anyone with a little _chutzpah_ is free to be whoever they want to be, do whatever they want to do, and achieve more than they ever dreamed.
In 1993, I joined the Navy to defend those freedoms.
In 2018, I ran for Congress to expand them.
In 2020, I won re-election to continue that work, making our nation free, safe, and prosperous.
In 2022, I served on the January 6th Committee because our Constitutional freedoms were threatened.
In 2026, I’m running for Congress again, because our current representative either _can’t_ or _won’t_ protect them.
The fact is that Coastal Virginia is in crisis. Our community’s been hit hard by this president’s failed agenda. **It’s time for action.**
Flipping Virginia’s Second District won’t be easy. Dark money groups and super PACs are watching closely, trying to see if we’re strong enough to pose a real threat. **This will be one of the toughest fights of the 2026 election cycle.**
Luckily, _chutzpah_ runs in my family. I’m not afraid of a little _mishigas._ And with you behind me, I’m ready to be the unapologetic champion Virginia families need.
[**Will you split a $25 donation between my campaign and Blue Amp Action to help me win this battleground race and restore America’s promise for ALL?**](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/11036?source=LOC_EM_FR_2026.05.20_Luria-Chutzpah_B2_F1_S15_C15_90AC-365DON_RS-T0&t=7&akid=2299%2E259176%2EBHv849)

Not only did he remove me from my position as Chief of the Navy Reserve after 35 years of service, but he’s actively undermining the foundation of our military. name: Pou HQ
subject: Is your utility bill rising?
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP61/1/115406/images/pout-header-3.png]

Friend,

Have you noticed your utility bills rising lately? You're not alone.

Families across New Jersey are feeling the squeeze every single month. From utilities to gas to groceries, costs are rising across the board. And it's all because of MAGA doubling down on failed policies. They promised to lower costs, but instead they gave us chaos, corruption, and policies that make life more expensive.

It doesn't have to be this way. We can do something about this, and it starts right here in this district.

Nellie has been a steadfast advocate for us in Congress. She's pushed for affordability, protected working families, and shown up for this community time and time again. Now, she's running for re-election to keep fighting for us, but MAGA is targeting her seat and getting ready to pour dark money into this race because they know the path to the House majority runs right through our district.

We need your help to re-elect Nellie, take back the House, and bring costs down. Will you pitch in to join our team today? [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/pou_em?refcode=260519_hq_utility_l1]

PITCH IN [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/pou_em?refcode=260519_hq_utility_b2]

Thank you for standing with us.

— Pou HQ
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP61/1/115406/images/pou_headshot_crop.jpg]

About Nellie Pou
Nellie Pou is the first Latina to represent New Jersey in Congress, and will be a target for the NRCC in 2026. Friend, Tennessee Republicans think they scored a victory when they voted to carve up Memphis and dismantle the last Democratic stronghold in our state. _I think they may have made the biggest political miscalculation Tennessee has seen in years._ Because what they did was not the act of a confident party. It was the act of a party that is scared of the power sitting right here in Shelby County. They did not redraw these maps because Memphis is weak. _They redrew these maps because Memphis is strong._ The fact is Shelby County remains home to**four hundred thousand active voters**. That means even after years of voter suppression, disinvestment, and political attacks, this county still has the numbers to change the future of Tennessee. **That is exactly why they are trying so hard to divide us.** The new maps split Shelby County into multiple Republican-leaning districts after lawmakers dismantled Tennessee’s only Democratic and majority-Black congressional district. But here is what the architects of this power grab do not want people to realize: _**Even these newly drawn districts are not untouchable.**_ Political analysts may rate them R+20 today. But if Shelby County voters fully mobilized, if turnout surged in Memphis neighborhoods that have too often been ignored or discouraged, even those districts could become competitive. _**This is not fantasy. It is a fact**_ \- backed by actual votes. We are watching political earthquakes happen all over the country. Since Donald Trump’s most recent election, we have seen Democratic candidates overperform even in deep red states and conservative districts where pundits swore it was impossible, **often by double digits. We have seen voters reject extremism, reject chaos, and reject politicians who believe power belongs to them instead of the people - even when the democratic candidate was outspent 10 to 1.** Because pundits don’t vote. Money doesn’t vote. People do. And the people are waking up. Shelby County is not some powerless corner of Tennessee. For generations, “Big Shelby” helped shape the direction of state politics. Memphis was a center of political, economic, and cultural power. Leaders across Tennessee understood that if Shelby County was organized and engaged, it could move the entire state. Republicans understand that history very well. That is why they are trying to fracture our political influence now. Make no mistake _\- this was intentional._ **They know Shelby County has the votes.** They also know the fastest-growing frustration in Tennessee is among working families tired of low wages, failing healthcare access, underfunded schools, attacks on voting rights, and politicians more focused on culture wars than real problems. And they know that if enough people in Memphis and Shelby County fully participate, the political map of Tennessee changes overnight. **So what was their strategy?**
* Suppress turnout.
* Create hopelessness.
* Convince people their vote no longer matters. Because then the voters will stay home.

But here is the truth they are desperate to hide -_**there is hope.**_ In the May 2026 primary alone, Shelby County Democrats increased turnout dramatically (over 60%) compared to 2018, while Republican participation fell sharply (120%). _**That should send shockwaves through Tennessee politics.**_ Because if that energy continues into 2026, this state becomes competitive again far sooner than the political establishment believes possible. **That means the path forward is clear.**
* Register voters.
* Organize neighborhoods.
* Knock doors.
* Talk to the people who have lost faith in politics.
* Fight for every inch of this state.

_**Shelby County is a sleeping giant.**_ And the GOP just made Memphis madder. Friends, I want to take a few minutes to talk to you about something incredibly important — California’s fentanyl crisis.
Fentanyl doesn’t discriminate between rich and poor or urban and rural. Right now, fentanyl addiction is devastating families in every corner of our state.
This crisis requires a comprehensive approach that addresses both public safety and public health:
1. We must investigate and prosecute fentanyl traffickers responsible for bringing this deadly drug into our state.
2. We need to educate young people about the dangers of fentanyl to prevent addiction in the first place.
3. And we need to support treatment and recovery for those struggling with substance use.
My office has secured more than $2 billion in funding from settlements with the opioid industry for their role in fueling the opioid crisis that helps fund addiction and education programs throughout our state.
Local, state, and federal law enforcement agencies are collaborating every day to fight the supply of fentanyl before the deadly drugs reach our communities, and we will continue to do so.
Last week, after a long-term investigation, we arrested a major trafficker in Arcadia, seizing 8.5 million potentially deadly doses of fentanyl.
Bottom line: If you traffic fentanyl in California, we will investigate you, we will stop your operations, and we will hold you accountable.
Arresting those responsible for the flow of fentanyl into our neighborhoods will save lives — but this fight goes beyond any single arrest. We will not relent in our ongoing work to confront the fentanyl crisis that is poisoning our communities, taking innocent lives, and tearing families apart.
Thank you for reading, and for supporting this important work.
—Rob

Attorney General of California

Donald Trump’s Supreme Court is complicit in Trump’s white supremacist and corrupt agenda.
Their decision in Louisiana v. Callais will allow Republican-majority states to redraw voting districts and disenfranchise people of color.
Simply put, Trump’s handpicked justices are helping turn back the clock on voting rights in America.
Republicans know they will lose this midterm—a time when voters speak their mind through their ballots—if they don’t cheat.
That’s why I’m proud to have stood in Montgomery, Alabama, at the “All Roads Lead to the South” National Day of Action Mass Rally, where I joined organizers, advocates, and communities from across the country to DEMAND federal voting rights protections, both in the streets and on the House floor.
We gathered in Montgomery, Alabama, walking in the footsteps of those who marched in 1965 to fight for a democracy that includes everyone ; something that still evades us sixty-one years later. [https://www.instagram.com/reel/DYavIs9NZNY/]
When the MAGA extremists and the GOP threaten anyone’s rights, they threaten everyone’s rights.
Add your name to my petition and tell the Republicans what you think about their war on our voting rights: [https://secure.ngpvan.com/T_nTWRqdi0qiuy6QL8ilFQ2]
SIGN THE PETITION [https://secure.ngpvan.com/T_nTWRqdi0qiuy6QL8ilFQ2]
Don’t forget, we already impeached Donald Trump twice . His MAGA extremists and the D.C. elites who bankroll them are afraid of Americans holding them accountable. They’re afraid of the very people they swore to represent and protect.
We must take back the majority. This is an all-hands-on-deck moment to protect our democracy.
The Oregon primary election is today , and if we flip the House and Senate this year, we can stop Trump’s corruption, defend our democracy, and fight back against the extremists who think our country is for sale. Crucially, we can codify voting rights to keep this corruption from ever happening again.
If you haven’t voted yet, you can find a drop box location here:
FIND A DROP BOX [https://sos.oregon.gov/voting/Pages/drop-box-locator.aspx]
If you already voted or are looking for another way to make your voice heard, share your opinion and sign our petition today: [https://secure.ngpvan.com/T_nTWRqdi0qiuy6QL8ilFQ2]
SIGN THE PETITION [https://secure.ngpvan.com/T_nTWRqdi0qiuy6QL8ilFQ2]
In solidarity,
Maxine Dexter

name: Mark Kelly
subject: Two House Candidates You Need To Watch
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Mark Kelly for Senate
body:
JoAnna Mendoza and Jonathan Nez.
#

Friend, it's Mark.
For all of us, taking back majorities in the House and Senate is incredibly important. It won’t be easy, though. The people running those races face a number of challenges. I know that all too well — my two campaigns for Senate were some of the most expensive in history.
It shouldn’t take millions and millions of dollars to run for Congress, but after Citizens United and the injection of unlimited donations from billionaires and corporate PACs, that’s the world we live in.
For my part, I’m going to do everything I can to level the playing field. So, today, I want to tell you about two candidates in Arizona that could determine which party controls the House next year.
JoAnna Mendoza and Jonathan Nez.
JoAnna is a former Marine Corps drill instructor, a single mom, and a critical voice for her community. She’s running in Arizona’s 6th Congressional District.
Jonathan is the former President of the Navajo Nation, the largest tribe in the country. He’s running in Arizona’s 2nd Congressional District.
Both are the exact kind of citizen leaders our country needs right now, and both have a really good chance of winning their races if they get the support they need.
We can make sure that happens, so I’m asking you to split a donation between their two campaigns.
[**If I can count on you to help two incredible candidates win their races in Arizona, please: Use this link and make a donation of $10 or anything you can afford — half will go to JoAnna, and the other half to Jonathan.**](https://act.markkelly.com/go/1389?c0=mek-em-mendoza-nez.qGBes6&refcode=em260519-1-60&t=1&akid=6463%2E6688874%2Eu4WlM0)

When Trump came into office last January, he was confronting a machine built to keep us unhealthy.
According to the D.C.-based nonprofit organization OpenSecrets, which tracks and publishes data on campaign finance and lobbying, Big Pharma and Big Food are among the most powerful lobbying groups in Washington, D.C.
They lobby politicians to protect their lucrative drug patents.
They lobby politicians to prevent us from having access to cheaper Canadian drugs.
They lobby on issues related to healthcare reform, drug pricing, and everything else that might affect their bottom line.
But their reign is ending under Trump 2.0.
Thanks to administration members like RFK Jr., we're seeing an unprecedented reform of American food and healthcare.
In fact, I'm having Grace Sesi, Jennifer Galardi, and Tiffany Ryder on the show tonight--6 pm ET-- to talk the latest in MAHA.
If you ask me, it's one of the biggest wins of the Trump administration thus far--and that's a pretty high bar.

| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/aaronregunberg/p/corporate-dems-are-climate-scapegoating?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

Corporate Democrats have spent the last year and a half trying to deflect blame for their party's 2024 losses away from themselves and towards their ideological opponents. Perhaps the most consistent target of these factional attacks has been the Democratic Party's commitment to climate action, with multiple billionaire-funded groups like [WelcomePAC](https://substack.com/redirect/0d080d7b-eb7c-42e2-883b-04e0f1f38d63?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [Searchlight Institute](https://substack.com/redirect/372983d8-d77d-4248-86ac-b1f5d67cd6b6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) issuing calls for Democrats to stop talking about climate change.
This [climate hushing](https://substack.com/redirect/ec677c27-c9ae-4ef2-bc4b-16998ddecb7d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) kicked into gear again recently, with a _New York Times_ [op-ed](https://substack.com/redirect/ea0a9adf-be32-40b6-a9d7-fef5223ca512?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (one of [many](https://substack.com/redirect/88073f56-b5d3-4a9c-b668-a550bf836836?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [such](https://substack.com/redirect/82cec29f-3a2d-4243-ba9b-680744663428?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [pieces](https://substack.com/redirect/87b96e05-3738-4621-bbdc-4470ac762d9c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the _Times_ has run in the last year) originally [titled](https://substack.com/redirect/680b879f-ac62-4079-aeea-9ea2c8a20766?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), "Forget Climate Change. Democrats Need to Talk About Other Issues," which argued that the "way out" of Democrats' current unpopularity is to "stop elevating" issues like climate. While that piece was going to press, centrist Democrats were [convening](https://substack.com/redirect/48fdcfce-37f9-492e-a8b7-23584f7e5c5b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Canada to discuss, among other topics, the need for "less climate talk." As Sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., said during the conference, "The average American is going to struggle to care about climate change if they can't figure out how to pay their rent."
The assumptions here are that climate action is deeply unpopular among American voters, that Democrats consistently put climate at the center of their messaging, and that that messaging is a major reason for their losses in 2024. But none of these assumptions are true.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..dhSwVXUvasSYSjKr7N1P6OTwCtbj4oi3_H906EhFzio?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=197552453)
A recent [Gallup poll](https://substack.com/redirect/c5a76a66-e6dd-4771-b658-23e3923208d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) found that climate concern is near an all-time high. A [2025 Pew Research Center poll](https://substack.com/redirect/20f79666-5749-4399-a884-4e28437a00d8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) found that a majority of Americans believe climate change is a major threat to the United States, while only 19 percent believe it is not a threat. And a series of peer-reviewed studies from the [89% Project](https://substack.com/redirect/2451b6cb-8de8-4104-b2c9-7e4b0e840abe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) found that 74 percent of voters in the U.S. want their government to "do more" about climate change.
As these numbers make clear, there is actually super-majority support for clean energy and climate action in this country. And no climate hushers have provided any evidence to the contrary. The best they have been able to show is that climate does not make the top of the list of most motivating issues to voters. But that makes sense: Climate shows up in people's lives not as an issue unto itself, but in the form of rising insurance costs, the health impacts from heatwaves, or a need for greater disaster preparedness.
Advocates have long known that the best way to talk about climate is in the context of people's everyday concerns. If Democrats were talking about climate in isolation, vaguely gesturing at the need to limit global temperature rise, and doing this to the exclusion of other issues that voters feel to be more pressing, no doubt that would be a mistake.
But here's the thing: Nobody--literally nobody--has been doing that. Democrats called their big Biden-era climate law the "Inflation Reduction Act." Kamala Harris [barely mentioned](https://substack.com/redirect/c76156ca-36d5-4035-8375-cf9d9a143d8d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) climate in her campaign. It's not like she refused to talk about rising rents because she was obsessed with the Green New Deal, as Slotkin's comment seems to imply. Indeed, [it's been](https://substack.com/redirect/371a90a8-34c6-4ad9-ab66-83a98ca04b38?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [well-reported](https://substack.com/redirect/2ddd2bb4-db9d-4919-855c-19ab3496698e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Harris was pushed to deemphasize her affordability agenda by corporate advisors and Wall Street donors, not climate activists. But corporate-backed Democratic politicians and think tanks see the climate movement as a much more convenient scapegoat.
In the 2024 election, climate simply wasn't an issue at all. Biden's age, the war in Gaza, inflation, and Harris's inability to articulate a clear vision for her presidency were all much more determinative factors. In fact, most voters [hadn't even heard of the Inflation Reduction Act](https://substack.com/redirect/bf1fd325-49e7-42f2-8ea1-16f814a305e3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--and when they were told about it, they loved it. That suggests that _more_ messaging on climate, not less, would have helped Harris and Democrats.
Indeed, climate change offers major political opportunities for the Democratic Party. Discussing climate action is a way for Democrats to simultaneously rally the base and win over moderates who [overwhelmingly](https://substack.com/redirect/06453654-bb80-436a-b1d0-168617f406c0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) trust Democrats more on this issue than Republicans. It's also a way to wedge the GOP: A [majority](https://substack.com/redirect/9de72cad-9554-4156-96c9-d4dd2e8859fc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of young Republicans care about climate, most [MAGA voters](https://substack.com/redirect/fce7e18f-16ef-4cea-b5f9-cc4249c63028?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) support solar, and the Make America Healthy Again wing of MAGA is concerned about the health impacts of fossil fuels (which is [worrying](https://substack.com/redirect/3b295810-04da-4b31-ad73-0ade87857fdd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) climate denialists).
Yes, Democrats need to be smart about connecting climate to affordability--something the IRA failed to do, with its long time horizons and indirect benefits that were removed from people's daily experiences. But this isn't rocket science. A [majority of voters](https://substack.com/redirect/ae762cfb-5583-4178-8314-816331a5563f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) say they believe climate change will have a direct financial impact on their families, and a [strong majority](https://substack.com/redirect/faa18a70-4963-4b40-bbb8-9a41e4357edf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of Americans are struggling with rising electricity prices, a problem that voters [primarily](https://substack.com/redirect/06453654-bb80-436a-b1d0-168617f406c0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) blame on corporate profits (38 percent), data centers (14 percent), and grid pressures from extreme weather (11 percent).
On the flip side, expanding clean energy is the fastest way to produce cheap electricity needed to lower utility rates--and Democrats hold a massive trust advantage over Republicans when it comes to clean power. By articulating how climate action can address these bread-and-butter concerns, in contrast with Republicans--for example: Democrats want to expand cheap, clean energy to secure lower utility rates, while Trump is spending [billions of taxpayer dollars](https://substack.com/redirect/afccbe21-d375-4a0d-870c-1a5a3183327c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to cancel these projects; Democrats want to make polluters pay for increasingly costly climate disasters, while Republicans [want us](https://substack.com/redirect/479cb6bc-665f-4aa1-ad27-5884b4281dfb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to pay for the damage Big Oil caused--Democrats can leverage their advantages on these issues to win voters' trust on some of working people's most significant affordability concerns.
These are not complicated ideas, as [populist](https://substack.com/redirect/018f11e9-043a-4f9e-a0de-6de8895a3e42?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) policy frameworks like the Climate and Community Institute's recent "[Stop Greed, Build Green](https://substack.com/redirect/c1f558f3-f025-4be7-8ab0-a6740d7c04d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" agenda make clear. And it's worth noting the element of class condescension that is woven into the climate hushers' apparent belief that working class voters are too stupid or poorly educated to care about these issues. In the recent _Times_ op-ed, the author claims that only highly educated and affluent voters--the "Brahmin Left"--prioritize climate action. This is factually incorrect--[polling](https://substack.com/redirect/11802868-d766-4bac-a76c-35289bc85500?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) has repeatedly shown that more Latino, Black, and lower-income people say climate change is important to their vote than rich white people do. The idea that the "little people" aren't sophisticated enough to care about a global crisis that they are disproportionately on the front lines of should be closely interrogated.
Finally, in addition to all these messaging considerations, we should not forget the substantive urgency of addressing climate change. Again and again in recent years, what had previously been considered [worst-case scenarios](https://substack.com/redirect/fa573690-7a71-494e-986b-55d62e2490a5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for the escalating speed and destructive effects of global warming have been proven, if anything, to be too conservative. [Record-breaking wildfires](https://substack.com/redirect/449cfef8-534e-45f9-856f-158996adceea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), extreme heat, and drought are already causing severe misery across vast swathes of our country, and the monstrous El Niño currently building up in the Pacific could literally [kill millions](https://substack.com/redirect/e0f31fce-ff9e-4a10-ae77-db6028035418?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
If we want safety and security for ourselves and our children, we need to take serious climate action. And we can't actually do that obliquely. Yes, clean energy economics are so good at this point that we're going to see a degree of decarbonization even without building an explicit pro-climate coalition. But this laissez-faire approach won't be enough to break through fossil fueled rightwing opposition--at least not at a speed and scale necessary to have a good shot at avoiding the most horrific climate outcomes that we are currently on track to experience.
Whether or not Democrats talk about climate, the other side certainly will--Fox News and the Koch network and the fossil fuel industry, flush with [war profiteering](https://substack.com/redirect/196068a5-f050-4805-aea1-d48002c8021e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) cash that can be funneled into lobbying campaigns to further rig the game against renewables, will keep spreading disinformation and polarizing against climate action. And in the absence of a potent social demand for that action, the political will for real decarbonization--in the face of obstacles, trade-offs, and entrenched opposition interests--risks collapsing.
There are lots of important questions and debates we can and should be having about how to rebuild an explicit popular climate discourse over time. But the argument that we shouldn't be trying to do that at all contradicts the polling data and is an argument for accepting climate catastrophe. That is something all people of good conscience should resist.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/49ed6858-e37d-4307-9d0a-14bf543575be?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

Mississippi did not invent the data center boom. But we did help invent the modern state level subsidy model for industrial recruitment. During the Great Depression, Mississippi's Balance Agriculture with Industry program became the first plan of its kind in the country. Other states copied it, and we have spent almost ninety years trying to win an arms race we helped start.
The story is worth telling, because the people writing checks in Jackson today sometimes act as if this is new. It is not.
Before Hugh White became governor, he was mayor of Columbia, Mississippi. During his time in office, White tried to bring industry to his hometown and to Marion County. He did it without state taxpayer money. He declared a holiday lasting two hours, called a community meeting, and asked local people to step up. Businessmen, secretaries, clerks, schoolteachers, and farmers signed promissory notes guaranteeing the funding for a factory building. With those pledges in hand, White used his own wealth and influence to secure a loan from New Orleans bankers.
The plant was built. The jobs came. The Columbia Plan became the talk of the state.
That, by the way, is much closer to capitalism than what Jackson does now. Local people put up local capital, of their own free will, behind a project they thought would pay off. No special session. No statewide tax holiday. No corporate welfare line item. The market, meaning actual citizens making actual decisions with their actual money, built the factory.
Then White ran for governor on the strength of the Columbia Plan. He won. And he immediately turned the model into something very different.
The 1936 Balance Agriculture with Industry program, BAWI for short, became Mississippi's first major experiment in state directed industrial recruitment. Under the Mississippi Industry Act of 1936, local governments could offer subsidies, grants, loans, and tax relief to entice manufacturers from higher wage northern states to relocate here. There was just one problem: the Mississippi Constitution explicitly prohibited the state from using public credit to finance industrial development.
White had to assemble a panel of attorneys to engineer a legal workaround. They linked BAWI to the constitution's general welfare clause and argued that industrial employment itself served the general welfare. Courts eventually upheld the arrangement. But that does not erase the larger point. Our state's own founding document was written to restrain this kind of public credit scheme, and Mississippi found a way around it.
BAWI created a new kind of economic development politics. The state would help decide which companies to recruit, and local governments would be expected to finance the incentives. For the first time, Mississippi was not just setting the rules of the game. It was helping pick the players.
And here is the most telling part: Mississippi canceled BAWI in 1940. The program had brought some factories and some jobs, but not enough to settle the argument. Only twelve manufacturing plants relocated under the program. Critics argued that the job numbers were overstated, that displacement was ignored, and that the cost per worker was too high. A 1944 evaluation by economist Ernest Hopkins credited BAWI with some benefits, but warned that the program itself was not the "fundamental or decisive factor" behind many of the gains claimed for it.
Translation: the subsidy did not do the work the press releases said it did.
That should sound familiar.
What changed over the next eighty years was not the logic. It was the size of the deals.
The Nissan vehicle plant came to Canton in 2003. The plant is real. The jobs are real. Nissan has reported 6,400 workers and a $400 million annual payroll. But the subsidy was real too. State and local governments offered Nissan more than $1.3 billion in incentives, infrastructure, borrowing costs, and tax relief. Using Nissan's own employment number, that works out to $203,125 in public subsidy per worker, more than three times the average annual payroll benefit per Nissan employee.
That does not mean the Nissan plant is bad. It means the public price of the plant matters.
And the job math matters too. An academic analysis by John Patrick Peavy found that 90 percent of the Mississippians employed at Nissan already lived and worked in the surrounding five county area when the plant opened. They were not pulled out of unemployment. Many were pulled away from other Mississippi employers. That is the part governors do not mention at ribbon cuttings. The new plant is what is seen. The existing businesses competing for the workers left behind are what is not seen.
Toyota in Blue Springs followed with a $354 million subsidy package. The plant opened, and it remains an important employer. But the indirect job promises used to sell the deal did not match reality. The state was promised 2,000 direct jobs and 6,300 supplier and indirect jobs. The direct job goal was met. The supplier and indirect jobs remained far below the projection.
Continental AG in Hinds County followed in 2016 with a roughly $600 million subsidy package, one of the largest in Mississippi history. That deal included state borrowing, state income and franchise tax breaks, local property tax breaks, and state income tax rebates. Again, the project was sold as transformational. Again, the public was asked to trust projections that almost no one would go back and audit years later.
There is a phrase the French economist Frederic Bastiat coined in 1850 for exactly this: "that which is seen, and that which is not seen." The plant in Canton is what is seen. The announcement ceremony is what is seen. The press release is what is seen. The Mississippi small businesses paying into the system, the public dollars not used elsewhere, the roads not repaired, the taxes not lowered, the local employers losing workers to a subsidized competitor, that is what is not seen.
The cumulative bill is staggering. According to research by Thomas Garrett and William Shughart in _Promoting Prosperity in Mississippi_ , state and local governments in Mississippi have provided nearly $3.8 billion in tax breaks, grants, and loans to private businesses since 2000. That is roughly $1,300 for every man, woman, and child in this state.
Think about that the next time the state tells you it cannot afford something.
We could have cut taxes for working families. We could have made broad based business tax reform available to every employer instead of special deals for a few. We could have improved roads, ports, workforce training, and site preparation in ways that benefit every industrial user. Instead, we built a system where the public pays up front, the company gets the benefit immediately, and taxpayers are left hoping the projections come true.
The data center deals are not a new idea. They are the latest chapter of a ninety year old book whose ending we already know.
Amazon's initial Madison County package included $44 million in direct subsidies and a $215.1 million state infrastructure loan, before counting longer running tax exemptions. xAI's Southaven campus is eligible for Mississippi's data center incentive program, which waives major state taxes for certified data centers. Compass Datacenters' Meridian project includes data center tax exemptions, a $4 million site grant, and eligibility for Advantage Jobs rebates that can return up to 90 percent of employee state income tax withholding for qualified jobs.
Same script. Bigger numbers. Same ribbon cuttings. Same promises that this time, somehow, the subsidy will pay for itself.
There is a way out, and it is not nostalgia.
Not every modern project can be financed by passing around promissory notes at a courthouse meeting. A $20 billion data center is not a shirt factory in 1920s Columbia. But the lesson of the Columbia Plan still matters: private capital should bear private risk, local communities should have real accountability, and state government should stick to the basics.
Keep taxes low for everyone. Make permitting fast and predictable. Build infrastructure that serves more than one company. Protect property rights. Enforce environmental rules fairly. Make Mississippi an easy place to do business without making taxpayers silent partners in every corporate deal.
That is the conservative answer. Not because it is anti growth, but because it is the only kind of growth that can last.
We have one more chance to get this right with the data center boom. Our great grandchildren will inherit either the bill or the lesson. I would like, this time, for them to inherit the lesson.

| | Welcome to our community spotlight series! My entire life, I've worked to do my part to build an El Paso that supports and empowers everyone. In doing so, I've had the honor of meeting countless luminaries who tirelessly work to uplift our community. Going forward, each month I will spotlight the community members and organizations committed to breathing joy and life into our rich community and celebrate their impact. To kick off this series, I am pleased to spotlight the incredible work **Annunciation House** does for Texas 16. This organization's mission is deeply personal to me, and I am incredibly humbled to be honored as one of the 2026 Voice of the Voiceless award recipients at their Solidarity Dinner on May 23. Since opening its doors in 1978, the Annunciation House has been a pillar of our community. They are guided by the philosophy that to experience the Gospel more deeply, one must recognize that Jesus demands solidarity with and among the poor, believing it is through the wounded poor and the oppressed that his redemption of the world is brought about. It is this mandate that guides the entirely volunteer-led team at Annunciation House as they serve the most vulnerable in the El Paso-Juarez border communities. For over four decades, they have provided emergency shelter, family reunification, hot meals, and so much more to more than 500,000 migrants, refugees, and immigrants fleeing severe political violence and upheaval. El Paso knows better than most how our immigration policies directly affect communities along the southern border, and it is a place where the developed and developing worlds are deeply intertwined. For many migrants, coming to the United States is an absolute last resort, born of necessity. For this reason, I am forever grateful for the selfless work of the Annunciation House. No matter how different our journeys, we can never lose sight of the fact that all people deserve to be met with compassion and humanity. **[I encourage everyone to visit their website to learn more about their mission](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/131694329/622003522/576472898?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MTY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwYzU3ZTYwYi1hMDUzLWYxMTEtOGVmMy0wMDBkM2ExNGI2ZDYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=7YqXry8uRgw7MBiCgC3xvJgUYD1vE_yYX0sOwiNt-uI=&emci=e2af0d4a-7750-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=0c57e60b-a053-f111-8ef3-000d3a14b6d6&ceid=14565883) **and how their team embodies the teaching that "The work is one's life, and the living is one's work." With gratitude, _Veronica_ |

Hi there — It’s Becca. Last week, I announced that I’m running for re-election. And this week? We’re already right back in the fight. **Because Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and HHS are reportedly looking at a plan to push the “deprescribing” of psychiatric medications — including medications like SSRIs that millions of Americans rely on to treat depression, anxiety, and other mental health conditions.** Let me be crystal clear when I say this: **Mental health care is health care.** And the decision to start, stop, or change psychiatric medication belongs exactly where it has always belonged: between a patient and their doctor. Not with RFK Jr. Not with politicians. And certainly not with some guy in Washington who thinks his personal opinions should outweigh your lived experience, your doctor’s training, and the science behind it all. **Nope. No thank you. Hard pass.** **And this is exactly why I need you with me in this re-election fight. Because when powerful people try to play politics with our health care, I’m not going to sit quietly and hope it all works out. I’m going to push back, demand answers, and fight like hell for the people who need care.** [_**If you’re with me here, will you click this link and chip in today to help keep me in fights JUST like this one?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/131694736/622004583/-878768453?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5YzkwZmY0OC1hMDUzLWYxMTEtOGVmMy0wMDBkM2ExNGI2ZDYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=G6DL4kxr3FbiYhK0ERxINJQzVEkm2ECkfCbCcGn66KI=) So, I led a group of lawmakers demanding answers from HHS because this is dangerous. It risks confusing patients. It risks adding even more stigma to mental health care. And it risks people abruptly stopping medications that may be essential, stabilizing, even life-saving. **We have actual problems to solve instead of attacking science.** People can’t find therapists. Appointments are months out. Rural communities are losing providers. Care is too expensive. Insurance companies make people jump through flaming hoops — yes, flaming hoops — just to get treatment covered. Those are the problems HHS should be focused on. Not undermining trust in mental health care. Not putting pressure on people to go off medication. Not treating psychiatric care like some ideological playground. I’m in Congress to fight for people who are tired of being treated like political props. I’m here for the parent trying to get care for their kid. The veteran who finally found a medication that helps. The young person who is hanging on because they finally have support. The neighbor, the teacher, the farmer, the nurse, the friend who deserves dignity and care. **And I’ll tell you something else: I can fight like hell because people like you have my back**. Last week, I launched my re-election campaign. This week, I’m taking on RFK Jr. and HHS because they’re messing around with people’s mental health care — and that is exactly the kind of fight I came to Congress for. When people’s health and safety are on the line, you show up. You tell the truth. You throw your shoulders into the work. **That’s the job. That’s the fight. Truly. Groceries are ridiculous. Rent is ridiculous. Everything feels like it costs eleven dollars more than it did five minutes ago. **But if you’re able to chip in today, it sends a message: We’re not going to let this administration play politics with people’s mental health care. We’re not going to let stigma drive policy. And we’re not going to sit quietly while patients are put at risk.** **[CHIP IN TODAY!](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/131694738/622004585/-878768453?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5YzkwZmY0OC1hMDUzLWYxMTEtOGVmMy0wMDBkM2ExNGI2ZDYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=G6DL4kxr3FbiYhK0ERxINJQzVEkm2ECkfCbCcGn66KI=)** This is why elections matter. This is why we build people-powered campaigns. This is why I’m running again. Because when the people in power come for our health care, our freedoms, our dignity, or our kids — we fight back. **With compassion. With facts. Donald Trump’s second term has been defined by rising prices, Republican self-dealing, and cuts to Americans’ social safety nets. And instead of addressing any of these problems, Trump has made one thing clear: one of his administration’s top priorities before the midterms is passing the SAVE Act into law.

The SAVE Act is a dangerous, anti-democratic bill that would require American citizens to show documents like a birth certificate or passport just to register to vote. Republicans claim this legislation is intended to keep non-citizens from voting in federal elections, but that’s already a federal crime.

In reality, the SAVE Act is a plan to suppress the voices of countless eligible voters — including the approximately 69 million American women who have taken their spouse’s last name and trans people who have updated their legal name. Under the SAVE Act, anyone whose documents don't perfectly match would be forced to jump through even more hoops just to exercise their fundamental right to vote.

Donald Trump forced his allies to squeeze the SAVE Act through the U.S. House with their razor-thin majority. Now, he’s pressuring U.S. Senate Republicans to make it law because he’s scared of losing control in Congress.

**[Peter, will you support the EMILYs List women running to fight Trump’s dangerous agenda and defend the right to vote?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/131695448/622006154/-1282862128?refcode=WUEFEQ46_20260519_MaySaveAct_ALL_v1s4&sourceid=1058806&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNRUwvMS84NzA2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlMjQ2MGYzYS1hMTUzLWYxMTEtOGVmMy0wMDBkM2ExNGI2ZDYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=TwSMW2lG-TN5_XbkSoVmKGu10fsE1VglTy7n8dyQfLI=)** | [DONATE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/131695449/622006155/-1282862128?refcode=WUEFEQ46_20260519_MaySaveAct_ALL_v1s4&sourceid=1058806&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNRUwvMS84NzA2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlMjQ2MGYzYS1hMTUzLWYxMTEtOGVmMy0wMDBkM2ExNGI2ZDYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=TwSMW2lG-TN5_XbkSoVmKGu10fsE1VglTy7n8dyQfLI=)

The SAVE Act would give the election deniers and Trump loyalists sweeping new power over states’ election administration. It would sow confusion, undermine election security, and override states’ own election laws — even Utah’s Republican lieutenant governor admitted that the bill would hurt voters and be “impossible to implement.”

But that hasn’t stopped Republican governors and legislators from pushing copycat bills to earn Trump’s approval. Republicans in Arkansas and Kansas have introduced bills mirroring the SAVE Act’s voter suppression measures, and MAGA Republicans in Alaska and Michigan are working to force ballot measures that would bring the same anti-democratic restrictions to future elections.

**This has only made our mission to elect Democratic women at every level of government more crucial than ever.**

Here at EMILYs List, we endorse battle-tested leaders who will always stand up for their constituents’ fundamental rights and freedoms. Unlike Trump loyalists, EMILYs List women show up in their communities, listen to voters’ needs, and respond with clear plans of action — and they’re ready to take on Republicans from the state House to the U.S. House.

clean_body: Trump's top priority? Voter suppression. | = Peter, Donald Trump’s second term has been defined by rising prices, Republican self-dealing, and cuts to Americans’ social safety nets. And instead of addressing any of these problems, Trump has made one thing clear: one of his administration’s top priorities before the midterms is passing the SAVE Act into law. The SAVE Act is a dangerous, anti-democratic bill that would require American citizens to show documents like a birth certificate or passport just to register to vote. Republicans claim this legislation is intended to keep non-citizens from voting in federal elections, but that’s already a federal crime. In reality, the SAVE Act is a plan to suppress the voices of countless eligible voters — including the approximately 69 million American women who have taken their spouse’s last name and trans people who have updated their legal name. Under the SAVE Act, anyone whose documents don't perfectly match would be forced to jump through even more hoops just to exercise their fundamental right to vote. Donald Trump forced his allies to squeeze the SAVE Act through the U.S. House with their razor-thin majority. Now, he’s pressuring U.S. Senate Republicans to make it law because he’s scared of losing control in Congress. = | = The SAVE Act would give the election deniers and Trump loyalists sweeping new power over states’ election administration. It would sow confusion, undermine election security, and override states’ own election laws — even Utah’s Republican lieutenant governor admitted that the bill would hurt voters and be “impossible to implement.” But that hasn’t stopped Republican governors and legislators from pushing copycat bills to earn Trump’s approval. Republicans in Arkansas and Kansas have introduced bills mirroring the SAVE Act’s voter suppression measures, and MAGA Republicans in Alaska and Michigan are working to force ballot measures that would bring the same anti-democratic restrictions to future elections. This has only made our mission to elect Democratic women at every level of government more crucial than ever. Here at EMILYs List, we endorse battle-tested leaders who will always stand up for their constituents’ fundamental rights and freedoms. Unlike Trump loyalists, EMILYs List women show up in their communities, listen to voters’ needs, and respond with clear plans of action — and they’re ready to take on Republicans from the state House to the U.S. House. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue, your donation will go through immediately: = | = ---|--- = | = = | = Thank you, The EMILYs List team | = | | | | | ---|---|---|---|--- Thank you for being a supporter of EMILYs List.
